papers.title: End-to-End Training of Deep Visuomotor Policies
papers.pitch: This paper introduces a method for training deep visuomotor policies that map raw camera images directly to motor torques, enabling robots to learn complex manipulation tasks end-to-end.

papers.title: WebGPT: Browser-assisted question-answering with human feedback
papers.pitch: This paper introduces a system that fine-tunes GPT-3 to answer long-form questions by interacting with a text-based web-browsing environment, allowing the model to search the web, navigate pages, and collect references in support of its answers.

papers.title: Do As I Can, Not As I Say: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances
papers.pitch: This paper introduces SayCan, a method that combines large language models with robotic affordance functions to enable a mobile manipulator to execute abstract, long-horizon natural language instructions in real-world environments.

papers.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
papers.pitch: This paper introduces ReAct, a prompting paradigm that synergizes reasoning and acting in large language models by interleaving the generation of verbal reasoning traces with task-specific actions (e.g., decomposing a question into subgoals while searching Wikipedia, or tracking subgoal completion while navigating a simulated household).

papers.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
papers.pitch: Toolformer finetunes a pretrained LM to autonomously decide when, which, and how to call simple text-based APIs (search, QA, calculator, translation, calendar) by self-generating candidate calls and keeping only those that measurably reduce next-token loss. This lets a single model combine fluent language generation with reliable external computation and retrieval—improving zero-shot factual, math

papers.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Reflexion, a novel framework that reinforces language agents through linguistic feedback rather than weight updates — converting binary or scalar environmental rewards into verbal self-reflections stored in an episodic memory buffer to guide better decision-making in subsequent trials.

papers.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
papers.pitch: This paper introduces generative agents—computational software agents that produce believable simulacra of human behavior by combining a large language model (ChatGPT) with a novel architecture for long-term memory and reasoning—and deploys twenty-five such agents in a Sims-inspired sandbox environment called Smallville.

papers.title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
papers.pitch: This paper introduces VOYAGER, the first LLM-powered embodied lifelong learning agent that continuously explores, acquires diverse skills, and makes novel discoveries without human intervention in Minecraft.

papers.title: DeepSpeed-Chat: Easy, Fast and Affordable RLHF Training of ChatGPT-like Models at All Scales
papers.pitch: DeepSpeed-Chat introduces a unified system that implements a full three-stage RLHF training pipeline—supervised fine-tuning, reward model training, and PPO-based reinforcement learning—replicating the InstructGPT recipe while delivering the DeepSpeed Hybrid Engine, a single infrastructure that seamlessly transitions between inference mode (using tensor parallelism and optimized transformer ker

papers.title: Retroformer: Retrospective Large Language Agents with Policy Gradient Optimization
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Retroformer, a principled framework for reinforcing large language agents by learning a plug-in retrospective model that automatically tunes language agent prompts from environment feedback through policy gradient optimization — specifically fine-tuning a smaller local LM (LongChat-7b) to generate verbal self-reflections that summarize the root causes of prior failed atte

papers.title: Studying Large Language Model Generalization with Influence Functions
papers.pitch: This paper introduces an efficient approach to scaling influence functions up to large language models with up to 52 billion parameters by using the Eigenvalue-corrected Kronecker-Factored Approximate Curvature (EK-FAC) approximation to compute inverse-Hessian-vector products (IHVPs) orders of magnitude faster than traditional iterative methods while maintaining comparable accuracy.

papers.title: Everything of Thoughts: Defying the Law of Penrose Triangle for Thought Generation
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Everything of Thoughts (XOT), a thought prompting framework that combines Monte Carlo Tree Search guided by lightweight policy/value networks with LLM-based thought revision to generate cognitive mappings for complex problem-solving.

papers.title: System 2 Attention (is something you might need too)
papers.pitch: This paper introduces System 2 Attention (S2A), a technique that leverages an LLM's own instruction-following and natural language reasoning abilities to regenerate the input context, stripping out irrelevant or opinionated portions before attending to that cleaned context to produce the final response.

papers.title: ReST meets ReAct: Self-Improvement for Multi-Step Reasoning LLM Agent
papers.pitch: This paper introduces ReST meets ReAct, a method that applies Reinforced Self-Training (ReST)–style iterative self-improvement to a process-based ReAct LLM agent for multi-step web-search question answering, using the PaLM 2 model family and composing synthetic trajectories with AI feedback as a ranking reward model rather than human labels.

papers.title: The Hedgehog & the Porcupine: Expressive Linear Attentions with Softmax Mimicry
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Hedgehog, a learnable linear attention mechanism that closes the performance gap between standard softmax attention and prior linear attentions by explicitly training feature maps to mimic softmax attention weights, recovering two absent properties—low-entropy "spikiness" (selective, non-uniform weighting of relevant tokens) and dot-product monotonicity (attention weights

papers.title: Fiddler: CPU-GPU Orchestration for Fast Inference of Mixture-of-Experts Models
papers.pitch: This paper proposes Fiddler, a resource-efficient inference system for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models running on heterogeneous CPU-GPU architectures with limited GPU memory.

papers.title: Stream of Search (SoS): Learning to Search in Language
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the Stream of Search (SoS) framework, a method for teaching language models to perform search — including exploration, backtracking, and recovery from mistakes — by representing the entire search process as a flattened string of text.

papers.title: T-MAC: CPU Renaissance via Table Lookup for Low-Bit LLM Deployment on Edge
papers.pitch: T-MAC introduces a lookup table (LUT)-based method for efficient low-bit LLM inference on CPUs, transforming the dominant data-type-centric multiplication into bit-wise table lookup to directly support mixed-precision matrix multiplication (mpGEMM) without dequantization.

papers.title: MindSearch: Mimicking Human Minds Elicits Deep AI Searcher
papers.pitch: This paper introduces MindSearch, an LLM-based multi-agent framework for complex web information seeking and integration that models human problem-solving as a dynamic graph construction process.

papers.title: Self-Taught Evaluators
papers.pitch: This paper proposes a scalable approach to train LLM-based evaluators without any human annotated preference data, using purely synthetic training data in an iterative self-improvement loop.

papers.title: B-STaR: Monitoring and Balancing Exploration and Exploitation in Self-Taught Reasoners
papers.pitch: This paper analyzes the dynamics of self-improvement training for LLMs on reasoning tasks—specifically mathematical problem-solving (MATH, GSM8K with Mistral-7B), coding (APPS with Llama3-8B), and commonsense reasoning (ARC-Challenge)—by identifying and monitoring two pivotal factors: exploration (the model's ability to generate sufficiently diverse correct responses, measured via Pass@K-S) an

papers.title: rStar-Math: Small LLMs Can Master Math Reasoning with Self-Evolved Deep Thinking
papers.pitch: This paper introduces rStar-Math, a self-evolvable System 2 reasoning approach that enables small language models (SLMs) to achieve frontier-level math reasoning by exercising "deep thinking" through Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS), where a math policy SLM performs test-time search guided by an SLM-based process reward model.

papers.title: Transformer-Squared: Self-adaptive LLMs
papers.pitch: The paper introduces Transformer², a two-pass self-adaptation framework that adapts frozen LLMs at inference by scaling singular values of weight matrices via compact per-layer “expert” vectors (SVF) trained with RL, enabling dynamic task-specific behavior without full fine-tuning. papers.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
papers.pitch: This paper introduces DeepSeek-R1-Zero and DeepSeek-R1, demonstrating that large-scale reinforcement learning (including a “pure RL” setup without supervised fine-tuning) can elicit long, self-verifying chain-of-thought reasoning and dramatically boost performance on hard reasoning benchmarks. papers.title: The AI Scientist-v2: Workshop-Level Automated Scientific Discovery via Agentic Tree Search
papers.pitch: This paper introduces The AI Scientist-v2, an end-to-end agentic system for automated scientific discovery that produces the first entirely AI-generated peer-review-accepted workshop paper.

papers.title: Multiverse: Your Language Models Secretly Decide How to Parallelize and Merge Generation
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Multiverse, a natively parallel generative modeling framework that internalizes a MapReduce paradigm—adaptively decomposing tasks (Map stage), executing subtasks in parallel (Process stage), and synthesizing results without information loss (Reduce stage)—to overcome the inherently sequential bottleneck of autoregressive LLMs.

papers.title: Language Modeling by Language Models
papers.pitch: The paper presents Genesys, a multi-agent LLM system that autonomously discovers novel autoregressive LM block architectures by simulating research stages (proposal, literature-backed design, unit-by-unit code generation, and laddered verification) inside a purpose-built environment (LMADE). papers.title: AutoTriton: Automatic Triton Programming with Reinforcement Learning in LLMs
papers.pitch: This paper introduces AutoTriton, the first model dedicated to Triton programming powered by reinforcement learning, built on Seed-Coder-8B-Reasoning through a sequential two-stage process—supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on a high-quality data gathering pipeline that produces <instruction, Triton code with CoT> pairs, followed by reinforcement learning with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRP

papers.title: Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models
papers.pitch: This paper introduces ACE (Agentic Context Engineering), a framework that treats LLM input contexts as evolving playbooks that accumulate, refine, and organize strategies through a modular process of generation, reflection, and curation — rather than compressing them into concise summaries.

papers.title: Demystifying Reinforcement Learning in Agentic Reasoning
papers.pitch: This paper conducts a systematic empirical investigation to demystify reinforcement learning for agentic reasoning across three axes—data, algorithm, and reasoning mode—using GRPO-based policy optimization on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 models evaluated on AIME2024/2025, GPQA-Diamond, and LiveCodeBench-v6.

papers.title: Scaling Agent Learning via Experience Synthesis
papers.pitch: This paper introduces DreamGym, a unified framework that trains LLM-based agents with scalable, reasoning-driven synthetic experiences—using a chain-of-thought experience model, a replay buffer grounded in offline trajectories, and curriculum task generation—to produce consistent state transitions and informative rewards for online RL. By replacing costly real-environment rollouts with controllabl

papers.title: DRIVE: Data Curation Best Practices for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Reward in Competitive Code Generation
papers.pitch: This paper studies how to construct RLVR datasets and design training curricula for competitive-programming code generation, implementing a two-stage pipeline on Qwen2.5-32B that combines supervised fine-tuning distilled from strong open-source models with reinforcement learning using executable, testcase-driven rewards.

papers.title: What Does It Take to Be a Good AI Research Agent? Studying the Role of Ideation Diversity
papers.pitch: The paper identifies and quantifies ideation diversity—the variety of initial model/architecture ideas an agent proposes—as a key bottleneck for LLM-driven AI research agents, using a large-scale analysis of 11,000 trajectories on MLE-bench and a controlled prompt intervention that causally reduces diversity and harms performance. papers.title: CUDA-L2: Surpassing cuBLAS Performance for Matrix Multiplication through Reinforcement Learning
papers.pitch: This paper introduces CUDA-L2, an LLM-guided reinforcement learning system that automatically generates and optimizes half-precision HGEMM CUDA kernels by using measured CUDA execution speed as the reward, exploring 1,000 (M,N,K) configurations. By systematically discovering tiling, pipelining, prefetching, and other low-level optimizations, CUDA-L2 delivers consistent speedups over torch.matmul a

papers.title: Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems
papers.pitch: This paper derives quantitative scaling principles for LM-based agent systems, identifying how agent count, coordination topology, model capability, and task properties interact to predict when multi-agent coordination helps or hurts. papers.title: Confucius Code Agent: Scalable Agent Scaffolding for Real-World Codebases
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the Confucius Code Agent (CCA) and the Confucius SDK—an AX/UX/DX‑driven agent scaffold that combines a lightweight orchestrator, hierarchical working memory with adaptive context compression, persistent note‑taking, modular extensions, and a meta‑agent build–test–improve loop to enable reliable, long‑horizon code reasoning over large repositories. papers.pitch: QwenLong-L1.5 presents a complete post-training recipe that turns a 30B long-context base model into a robust long-range reasoner by unifying a scalable long-context data synthesis pipeline, stabilized reinforcement-learning techniques (including AEPO and task-aware advantage estimation), and a memory-agent architecture that extends reasoning to inputs up to millions of tokens. papers.title: DEER: Draft with Diffusion, Verify with Autoregressive Models
papers.pitch: The paper introduces DEER, a lossless speculative decoding framework that drafts entire token blocks using a discrete diffusion LLM (dLLM) and then verifies them with a standard autoregressive (AR) model, replacing sequential AR drafters with one-step parallel generation. papers.pitch: Nemotron 3 Nano introduces a hybrid Mamba–Transformer with sparse Mixture-of-Experts (31.6B total params, ~3.2B active per pass) plus a large-scale pretraining and multi-stage post-training pipeline (SFT + RLVR + RLHF) to deliver strong reasoning and agentic tool-use while greatly improving inference throughput. papers.pitch: Nemotron 3 introduces a family of open models (Nano, Super, Ultra) that combine a hybrid Mamba–Transformer Mixture-of-Experts architecture with hardware-aware LatentMoE, Multi-Token Prediction, NVFP4 training, and multi-environment RL post-training to deliver high accuracy while dramatically improving inference throughput and scaling context to 1M tokens. papers.pitch: KernelEvolve is a production-grade agentic system that automatically generates, debugs, profiles, and optimizes Triton kernels across heterogeneous accelerators (NVIDIA, AMD, and Meta’s MTIA) by framing kernel synthesis as graph-based search guided by execution feedback and retrieval-augmented hardware knowledge. papers.title: Web World Models
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the Web World Model (WWM), a hybrid architecture that uses deterministic web code to implement world state and physics while leveraging large language models to generate contextual descriptions, narratives, and high-level content on top. papers.title: Agentic Reasoning for Large Language Models
papers.pitch: This survey synthesizes and formalizes the paradigm of Agentic Reasoning, organizing it into a three-layer taxonomy—foundational single-agent capabilities, self-evolving adaptation, and collective multi-agent coordination—and analyzing each layer through the complementary lenses of in-context reasoning (scaling test-time interaction via structured orchestration, e.g., ReAct-style interleaving

papers.title: Kimi K2.5: Visual Agentic Intelligence
papers.pitch: This technical report introduces Kimi K2.5, an open-source multimodal agentic model that jointly optimizes text and vision through a series of training techniques—joint text-vision pre-training (early fusion at a constant, moderate vision-to-text ratio rather than late-stage injection), zero-vision SFT (activating visual reasoning and tool use from text-only supervised data, without hu

papers.title: Search-R2: Enhancing Search-Integrated Reasoning via Actor-Refiner Collaboration
papers.pitch: This paper proposes Search-R2, an Actor–Refiner collaboration framework that enhances search-integrated reasoning in LLMs by decomposing generation into an Actor that produces initial reasoning trajectories and a Meta-Refiner that selectively diagnoses and repairs flawed steps via a “cut-and-regenerate” mechanism — surgically truncating at the point of error and regenerating the suffix rather

papers.title: Dr. Kernel: Reinforcement Learning Done Right for Triton Kernel Generations
papers.pitch: This paper systematically studies reinforcement learning for Triton kernel code generation, developing a robust distributed GPU environment—KERNELGYM—that enables long-horizon RL training with execution-based reward hacking checks, profiling feedback, and multi-turn data collection.

papers.title: Step 3.5 Flash: Open Frontier-Level Intelligence with 11B Active Parameters
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Step 3.5 Flash, a sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model with 196B total parameters and only 11B active per token, designed to deliver frontier-level agentic intelligence while minimizing inference latency and cost for real-world industrial deployment.

papers.title: Decoding ML Decision: An Agentic Reasoning Framework for Large-Scale Ranking System
papers.pitch: This paper introduces GEARS (Generative Engine for Agentic Ranking Systems), a framework that reframes large-scale ranking optimization as an autonomous discovery process within a programmable experimentation environment, evaluated across 20 internal experiments with 100 synthesized policy-selection instructions using Claude Sonnet as the backbone LLM.

papers.title: CUDA Agent: Large-Scale Agentic RL for High-Performance CUDA Kernel Generation
papers.pitch: This paper introduces CUDA Agent, a large-scale agentic reinforcement learning system that trains an LLM to generate high-performance CUDA kernels by jointly scaling data synthesis, a skill-augmented development environment with automated verification and profiling, and stability-oriented RL techniques.

papers.title: Qwen3-Coder-Next Technical Report
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Qwen3-Coder-Next, an open-weight 80-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model activating only 3 billion parameters per forward pass, designed for coding agents and real-world software development.

papers.title: Meta-Reinforcement Learning with Self-Reflection for Agentic Search
MolmoWeb: Open Visual Web Agent and Open Data for the Open Web
Human-level control through deep reinforcement learning
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the deep Q-network (DQN), a novel artificial agent that combines reinforcement learning with a deep convolutional neural network to learn control policies directly from high-dimensional sensory inputs — receiving only raw pixels and the game score — using end-to-end reinforcement learning.

papers.title: Online Convex Programming and Generalized Infinitesimal Gradient Ascent
papers.pitch: This paper introduces and formally defines online convex programming—a repeated optimization setting where a convex feasible set is known but the convex cost function at each step is revealed only after a decision is made—and proposes the Greedy Projection algorithm (projected gradient descent with a decreasing learning rate $\eta_t = t^{-1/2}$) to solve it.

papers.title: Efficient Selectivity and Backup Operators in Monte-Carlo Tree Search
papers.pitch: This paper introduces UCT (UCB applied to trees), a Monte-Carlo planning algorithm that uses the multi-armed bandit strategy UCB1 to guide selective action sampling during rollout-based lookahead search, treating action selection at each internal node as a separate bandit problem in which arms correspond to available actions and payoffs correspond to cumulative discounted rewards from sampled

papers.title: Cooperative Inverse Reinforcement Learning
papers.pitch: This paper introduces cooperative inverse reinforcement learning (CIRL), a game-theoretic framework that reformulates the value alignment problem as a cooperative, partial-information game where both human and robot share the human's unknown reward function.

papers.title: Inverse Reward Design
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the Inverse Reward Design (IRD) problem, which reframes a human-specified proxy reward function not as the ground-truth objective but as an observation about the true intended reward, to be interpreted in the context of the training MDP where it was designed.

papers.title: Fine-Tuning Language Models from Human Preferences
papers.pitch: This paper applies reward learning to fine-tune pretrained language models via reinforcement learning, using a reward model (a classifier trained to predict which of four candidate continuations a human prefers) to optimize policy outputs across four natural language tasks: stylistic continuation with positive sentiment or vivid descriptiveness, and summarization on the TL;DR and CNN/Daily Mai

papers.title: Recursively Summarizing Books with Human Feedback
papers.pitch: This paper proposes a method for scaling human feedback to tasks that are extremely time-consuming for humans to evaluate, targeting the difficult problem of abstractive summarization of entire fiction novels.

papers.title: Training a Helpful and Harmless Assistant with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
papers.pitch: This paper applies preference modeling and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) to fine-tune language models into helpful and harmless assistants.

papers.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Constitutional AI (CAI), a two-stage method for training a harmless AI assistant using only a small set of human-written principles — a constitution — instead of human feedback labels identifying harmful outputs.

papers.title: Self-Instruct: Aligning Language Models with Self-Generated Instructions
papers.pitch: This paper introduces SELF-INSTRUCT, a semi-automated framework for improving the instruction-following capabilities of pretrained language models by bootstrapping off their own generations—generating new task instructions and corresponding input-output instances from the model itself, filtering low-quality or repetitive outputs, and finetuning the original model on the resulting synthetic dat

papers.title: Preference Ranking Optimization for Human Alignment
papers.pitch: This paper proposes Preference Ranking Optimization (PRO), an efficient supervised fine-tuning algorithm that aligns LLMs with human preferences by extending pair-wise contrast to accommodate preference rankings of any length.

papers.title: RLCD: Reinforcement Learning from Contrastive Distillation for Language Model Alignment
papers.pitch: This paper proposes Reinforcement Learning from Contrastive Distillation (RLCD), a method for aligning language models to natural-language principles without human feedback — applied to harmlessness, helpfulness, and story outline generation using LLaMA-7B and LLaMA-30B.

papers.title: Open Problems and Fundamental Limitations of Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
papers.pitch: This paper surveys and taxonomizes open problems and fundamental limitations of Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) as applied to large language models, drawing on empirical evidence from deployed systems such as GPT-4, Claude, Bard, and Llama 2-Chat.

papers.title: Self-Alignment with Instruction Backtranslation
papers.pitch: This paper introduces instruction backtranslation, a scalable self-training method for building high-quality instruction-following language models without relying on distillation from stronger proprietary models.

papers.title: Statistical Rejection Sampling Improves Preference Optimization
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Statistical Rejection Sampling Optimization (RSO), a method for improving language model alignment with human preferences by constructing preference pairs from the estimated optimal policy rather than from the SFT policy or an unknown mixture of sources.

papers.title: Stabilizing RLHF through Advantage Model and Selective Rehearsal
papers.pitch: This paper introduces two techniques to stabilize Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) training for large language models.

papers.title: Safe RLHF: Safe Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
papers.pitch: This paper proposes Safe RLHF, a novel algorithm for aligning large language models with human values that explicitly decouples helpfulness and harmlessness into separate objectives—a reward model for helpfulness and a cost model for harmlessness—then formalizes safety as a constrained optimization problem solved via the Lagrangian method.

papers.title: Controlled Decoding from Language Models
papers.pitch: This paper introduces controlled decoding (CD), a modular inference-time framework that solves a tokenwise KL-regularized reinforcement learning objective to steer frozen language model generation toward higher-reward outcomes.

papers.title: The Unlocking Spell on Base LLMs: Rethinking Alignment via In-Context Learning
papers.pitch: This paper analyzes how alignment tuning—the process of supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF)—transforms base large language models into AI assistants, finding through token distribution shift analysis that alignment primarily affects stylistic tokens (discourse markers, safety disclaimers) rather than content-bearing words, with 92.2% of aligned-model

papers.title: Alignment for Honesty
papers.pitch: This paper proposes a systematic framework for alignment for honesty, which trains large language models to proactively refuse to answer questions when they lack knowledge while avoiding excessive conservatism.

papers.title: Helping or Herding? Reward Model Ensembles Mitigate but do not Eliminate Reward Hacking
papers.pitch: This paper analyzes whether reward model ensembles mitigate reward hacking—the phenomenon where language models exploit errors in reward models (RMs) to achieve high estimated reward without genuine quality improvement—across alignment at both training time (RLHF) and inference time (best-of-n reranking) on TL;DR, HELPFULNESS, and XSUM/NLI benchmarks using T5 models.

papers.title: Self-Rewarding Language Models
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Self-Rewarding Language Models, a framework where a single language model serves simultaneously as both the instruction-following policy and its own reward model via LLM-as-a-Judge prompting (evaluating candidate responses on a 5-point additive scale covering relevance, coverage, usefulness, clarity, and expertise).

papers.title: WARM: On the Benefits of Weight Averaged Reward Models
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Weight Averaged Reward Models (WARM), a strategy for combining multiple reward models (RMs) by averaging their weights in parameter space—rather than averaging their predictions at inference time—to serve as the proxy reward in RLHF.

papers.title: KTO: Model Alignment as Prospect Theoretic Optimization
papers.pitch: This paper proposes Kahneman-Tversky Optimization (KTO), a new alignment method for LLMs that directly maximizes the utility of generations—modeled through a Kahneman-Tversky human value function—instead of maximizing the log-likelihood of preferences as existing methods do (e.g., DPO).

papers.title: Direct Language Model Alignment from Online AI Feedback
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Online AI Feedback (OAIF), a method that makes direct alignment from preference (DAP) methods online and on-policy by using an LLM as an annotator — on each training iteration, two responses are sampled from the current policy and the LLM annotator chooses which is preferred, providing feedback without requiring a separately trained reward model.

papers.title: Teaching Large Language Models to Reason with Reinforcement Learning
papers.pitch: This paper studies how multiple reinforcement learning algorithms—Expert Iteration, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), and Return-Conditioned RL—improve LLM reasoning capabilities when using sparse, dense, or model-based rewards on GSM8K and SVAMP with Llama-2 7B and 13B models.

papers.title: Parameter Efficient Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
papers.pitch: This paper empirically studies whether Parameter Efficient Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (PE-RLHF) — applying LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) fine-tuning to both the reward model training phase and the reinforcement learning policy phase — can match the alignment quality of standard full-parameter RLHF while reducing computational cost.

papers.title: ChatGLM-Math: Improving Math Problem-Solving in Large Language Models with a Self-Critique Pipeline
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the Self-Critique pipeline, a weakly supervised iterative training framework that enhances both mathematical problem-solving and general language capabilities in LLMs without external supervisory models.

papers.title: Learn Your Reference Model for Real Good Alignment
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Trust Region alignment methods—TR-DPO, TR-IPO, TR-KTO—that dynamically update the reference policy during offline alignment training rather than keeping it fixed, using either soft updates (progressively blending the current policy into the reference at each step) or hard updates (periodically replacing the reference with a full copy of the current policy).

papers.title: Iterative Reasoning Preference Optimization
papers.pitch: This paper proposes Iterative Reasoning Preference Optimization (Iterative RPO), an iterative training algorithm that improves chain-of-thought reasoning by generating multiple candidate solutions, constructing preference pairs based on final-answer correctness, and training with a modified DPO loss augmented by a negative log-likelihood (NLL) term on the winning sequences.

papers.title: Self-Play Preference Optimization for Language Model Alignment
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Self-Play Preference Optimization (SPPO), an iterative fine-tuning method that treats language model alignment as a constant-sum two-player game and provably approximates the Nash equilibrium policy via multiplicative weight updates.

papers.title: Offline Regularised Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Models Alignment

papers.title: Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder-Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation

papers.title: Convolutional Neural Networks for Sentence Classification

papers.title: Memory Networks

papers.title: Neural Turing Machines

papers.title: Empirical Evaluation of Gated Recurrent Neural Networks on Sequence Modeling

papers.title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units

papers.title: Unsupervised Representation Learning with Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks

papers.title: DARTS: Differentiable Architecture Search

This innovation delivers unprecedented real-time speeds while generalizing well across domains, paving the way for responsive computer vision in autonomous vehicles, assistive techno

papers.title: Zero-Shot Text-to-Image Generation
papers.pitch: This paper introduces a simple yet powerful approach for generating images from natural language descriptions using a single, large-scale autoregressive transformer that models text and image tokens together. By combining a discrete VAE for compressing images and scaling training to 250 million text-image pairs with a 12-billion parameter model, the system achieves strong zero-shot performance, pr

papers.title: An Introduction to Conditional Random Fields
papers.pitch: This survey introduces conditional random fields (CRFs), a probabilistic framework for structured prediction that combines the representational power of undirected graphical models with the flexibility of discriminative classification to directly model the conditional distribution p(y|x) over output variables given input features.

papers.title: Deep Neural Networks for Acoustic Modeling in Speech Recognition
papers.pitch: This paper provides a shared overview of how four research groups replaced Gaussian mixture models (GMMs) with deep neural networks (DNNs) for acoustic modeling in automatic speech recognition across a variety of benchmarks—TIMIT, Bing Voice Search, Switchboard, Google Voice Input, YouTube, and English Broadcast News—using a two-stage training procedure.

papers.title: Deep learning
Web Search for a Planet: The Google Cluster Architecture
papers.pitch: This paper presents the architecture of Google's production search engine cluster, analyzing how a throughput-oriented, highly parallelizable workload enables a fundamentally different hardware procurement strategy from traditional enterprise computing.

papers.title: Conditional Image Generation with PixelCNN Decoders
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the Gated PixelCNN and its conditional variant, a convolutional autoregressive image model that generates pixels sequentially in raster-scan order.

papers.title: Deep Sparse Rectifier Neural Networks
papers.pitch: This paper studies how replacing the hyperbolic tangent activation function with the rectifier (`max(0, x)`) affects the training and performance of deep neural networks on image classification benchmarks (MNIST, CIFAR10, NISTP, NORB) and a sentiment analysis task (OpenTable restaurant reviews) using stacked denoising auto-encoders.

papers.title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
papers.pitch: This paper introduces a general end-to-end sequence-to-sequence learning method using multilayered Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks — one LSTM to encode the input sequence into a fixed-dimensional vector, and another deep LSTM to decode the target sequence from that vector — and applies it to the WMT'14 English-to-French machine translation task.

papers.title: StarCoder: may the source be with you!
papers.pitch: This paper introduces StarCoder and StarCoderBase, a pair of 15.5B-parameter open-access Code LLMs developed by the BigCode community and trained exclusively on permissively licensed source code from The Stack dataset.

papers.title: StarCoder 2 and The Stack v2: The Next Generation
papers.pitch: This technical report introduces StarCoder2, a family of open-weight Code LLMs at 3B, 7B, and 15B parameters, trained on The Stack v2—a new 900B+ token training corpus built from Software Heritage’s archive and supplementary high-quality sources including GitHub pull requests, Kaggle notebooks, and code documentation.

papers.title: Programming Every Example: Lifting Pre-training Data Quality Like Experts at Scale
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Programming Every Example (PROX), a framework that treats data refinement as a programming task by having small language models (as few as 0.3B parameters) generate and execute fine-grained operations—such as string normalization, line removal, and document filtering—for each individual example at scale.

papers.title: Coffee-Gym: An Environment for Evaluating and Improving Natural Language Feedback on Erroneous Code
papers.pitch: This paper introduces COFFEE-GYM, a comprehensive reinforcement learning environment for training open-source models that generate natural language feedback to guide code editing.

papers.title: CodeClash: Benchmarking Goal-Oriented Software Engineering
papers.pitch: Introduce CodeClash, a tournament-style benchmark where LMs act as persistent software‑engineering agents that iteratively edit codebases and compete in diverse “code arenas” toward open‑ended objectives. By running 1,680 tournaments across six arenas and eight models, the benchmark reveals that modern LMs can generate creative solutions but systematically fail at strategic reasoning, log‑driven a

papers.title: DataFlow: An LLM-Driven Framework for Unified Data Preparation and Workflow Automation in the Era of Data-Centric AI
papers.pitch: This paper introduces DataFlow, a unified LLM-driven framework for data preparation that elevates model-in-the-loop synthesis to a first-class, programmable abstraction through a PyTorch-style pipeline construction API.

papers.title: Adaptive Attention Span in Transformers
papers.pitch: This paper proposes a novel self-attention mechanism that learns an optimal attention span independently for each head, replacing the standard practice of assigning a uniform fixed context window across all attention heads.

papers.title: What Makes Good In-Context Examples for GPT-$3$?
papers.pitch: This paper studies how to optimally select in-context examples for GPT-3's few-shot learning, analyzing the sensitivity of GPT-3's performance to example choice on sentiment analysis, table-to-text generation, and open-domain question answering benchmarks using GPT-3.

papers.title: Train Short, Test Long: Attention with Linear Biases Enables Input Length Extrapolation
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Attention with Linear Biases (ALiBi), a position method that enables transformer language models to extrapolate to longer sequences at inference time without adding positional embeddings—instead, it biases attention scores with a linearly decreasing penalty proportional to query-key distance (e.g., a head-specific slope multiplies a static, non-learned bias matrix).

papers.title: Blockwise Parallel Transformer for Large Context Models
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the Blockwise Parallel Transformer (BPT), a memory-efficient architecture that computes both self-attention and the feedforward network in a fused blockwise manner — iterating over query blocks in an outer loop while processing key-value blocks in an inner loop to avoid materializing full intermediate tensors — to dramatically reduce the activation memory footprint of lar

papers.title: Augmenting Language Models with Long-Term Memory
papers.pitch: This paper introduces a framework called Language Models Augmented with Long-Term Memory (LONGMEM), which enables large language models to memorize and utilize long-form past contexts beyond their fixed input length limits.

papers.title: Extending Context Window of Large Language Models via Positional Interpolation
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Position Interpolation (PI), a method to extend the context window of RoPE-based pretrained LLMs by linearly down-scaling position indices to fit within the original pretrained range rather than extrapolating beyond it—which the authors show theoretically causes catastrophically high attention scores.

papers.title: Focused Transformer: Contrastive Training for Context Scaling
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the Focused Transformer (FOT), a technique that addresses what the authors identify as the distraction issue — the phenomenon where, as the number of documents in context increases, attention becomes evenly spread across relevant and irrelevant keys, degrading the model's ability to focus on pertinent information.

papers.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
papers.pitch: This paper empirically studies how current language models use long input contexts by analyzing performance on two tasks—multi-document question answering and synthetic key-value retrieval—across open (MPT-30B-Instruct, LongChat-13B) and closed (GPT-3.5-Turbo, Claude-1.3) models.

papers.title: In-context Autoencoder for Context Compression in a Large Language Model
papers.pitch: This paper proposes the In-context Autoencoder (ICAE), a method that leverages a large language model itself to compress long contexts into a small number of compact "memory slots" that can substitute for the original text when conditioning a target LLM.

papers.title: Lightning Attention-2: A Free Lunch for Handling Unlimited Sequence Lengths in Large Language Models
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Lightning Attention-2, the first linear attention implementation that realizes the theoretical computational benefits of linear attention in causal settings, where prior algorithms were bottlenecked by cumulative summation operations.

papers.title: Transformers are Multi-State RNNs
papers.pitch: This paper redefines decoder-only transformers as unbounded multi-state RNNs (MSRNNs) — a generalized RNN variant whose hidden state is a matrix that grows with each new token — and demonstrates that they can be converted into bounded MSRNNs by applying a compression policy to fix the size of their key-value cache.

papers.title: Resonance RoPE: Improving Context Length Generalization of Large Language Models
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Resonance RoPE, a modification to Rotary Position Embedding that improves length generalization in train-short-test-long (TSTL) scenarios by rounding each RoPE feature's wavelength to the nearest integer, eliminating the interpolation gap between in-distribution and out-of-distribution token positions on pre-critical dimensions.

papers.title: Leave No Context Behind: Efficient Infinite Context Transformers with Infini-attention
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Infini-attention, a new attention mechanism that enables Transformer-based LLMs to process infinitely long inputs with bounded memory and computation by incorporating a compressive memory into the standard attention layer — combining masked local attention (standard causal dot-product attention within each segment) and long-term linear attention (retrieving from an associ

papers.title: Reducing Transformer Key-Value Cache Size with Cross-Layer Attention
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Cross-Layer Attention (CLA), a modification to the transformer architecture that reduces the size of the key-value (KV) cache by sharing key and value activations across adjacent layers (e.g., a CLA2 configuration where every pair of consecutive layers reuses the same KV projections).

papers.title: GoldFinch: High Performance RWKV/Transformer Hybrid with Linear Pre-Fill and Extreme KV-Cache Compression
papers.pitch: This paper introduces GoldFinch, a hybrid Linear Attention/Transformer sequence model that combines an enhanced Finch (RWKV-6) architecture with a novel transformer variant called GOLD to achieve dramatic KV-cache compression — reducing cache size by 756–2550× relative to traditional transformers — while maintaining greater-than-Llama modeling performance.

papers.title: Transformers are Universal In-context Learners
papers.pitch: This paper proves that deep transformers are universal approximators of continuous in‑context mappings—functions mapping a token to an output conditioned on an arbitrarily large (even infinite) context—by modeling contexts as probability measures and using Wasserstein continuity. Crucially, the construction yields a single transformer that achieves any fixed precision without increasing embedding

papers.title: Writing in the Margins: Better Inference Pattern for Long Context Retrieval
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Writing in the Margins (WiM), a new inference pattern that exploits chunked prefill of the key-value cache to generate intermediate extractive summaries ("margins") at each segment boundary, which are then classified for relevance and reintegrated before the final prediction to improve long-context retrieval without fine-tuning.

papers.title: Selective Attention Improves Transformer
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Selective Attention, a simple parameter-free modification to the standard attention mechanism that enables tokens to reduce the attention future tokens pay to them by masking irrelevant prior elements from the context buffer.

papers.title: SeerAttention: Learning Intrinsic Sparse Attention in Your LLMs
papers.pitch: This paper introduces SeerAttention, a learnable attention mechanism that augments standard attention with a lightweight gating module—the Attention Gate (AttnGate)—which pools query and key tensors along the sequence dimension, processes them through linear layers, and predicts block-level sparsity to selectively activate important blocks in the attention map.

papers.title: KV Shifting Attention Enhances Language Modeling
papers.pitch: This paper introduces KV shifting attention, a modification to the standard transformer attention mechanism that decouples keys and values by blending each token's key and value with those of its preceding token, reducing the depth and width requirements for forming induction heads (the circuit that enables pattern matching, e.g., seeing "[A][B]" earlier in context and predicting "[B]" when "[

papers.title: Fourier Position Embedding: Enhancing Attention's Periodic Extension for Length Generalization
papers.pitch: This paper analyzes how Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) enables length generalization in LMs by revealing that RoPE implicitly performs Non-Uniform Discrete Fourier Transform on hidden states, creating periodic attention—but finds this periodicity is undermined by Spectrum Damage caused by linear layers and activation functions outside attention (spectrum leakage and distortion) as well as in

papers.title: MiniMax-01: Scaling Foundation Models with Lightning Attention
papers.pitch: MiniMax-01 presents a hybrid architecture that combines I/O‑aware linear “lightning attention” with intermittent softmax layers and a large Mixture‑of‑Experts design (456B params, 45.9B active) plus new parallelism and kernel optimizations to enable training with 1M‑token contexts and inference up to 4M tokens. This makes practical, single‑machine long‑context LLM/VLMs possible—unlocking book‑scal

papers.title: LongRoPE2: Near-Lossless LLM Context Window Scaling
papers.pitch: LongRoPE2 introduces a near-lossless method for extending the effective context window of pre-trained LLMs to a target length—128K in experiments—while preserving performance on the original shorter context window.

papers.title: Forgetting Transformer: Softmax Attention with a Forget Gate
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the Forgetting Transformer (FoX), a Transformer variant that incorporates a data-dependent forget gate into softmax attention by down-weighting unnormalized attention scores based on learned per-token scalar values—operationalized as an additive bias `D_ij = Σ log f_l` applied to the query-key logits before the softmax.

papers.title: Less Is More: Fast and Accurate Reasoning with Cross-Head Unified Sparse Attention
papers.pitch: This paper introduces LessIsMore, a training-free sparse attention mechanism designed explicitly for long-horizon reasoning workloads in large reasoning models.

papers.title: MetaEmbed: Scaling Multimodal Retrieval at Test-Time with Flexible Late Interaction
papers.pitch: This paper introduces MetaEmbed, a framework for multimodal retrieval that replaces conventional single-vector or patch-level multi-vector representations with a small set of learnable Meta Tokens whose last-layer hidden states serve as compact, contextualized embeddings for late interaction.

papers.title: InfLLM-V2: Dense-Sparse Switchable Attention for Seamless Short-to-Long Adaptation
papers.pitch: This paper introduces dense-sparse switchable attention (InfLLM-V2), a trainable sparse attention framework that enables LLMs to seamlessly adapt from short-sequence pretraining to long-sequence finetuning without introducing extra parameters—unlike prior approaches such as NSA, which require three separate KV projection sets and a gating module.

papers.title: DeepSeek-OCR: Contexts Optical Compression
papers.pitch: This paper proposes DeepSeek-OCR as an initial investigation into the feasibility of contexts optical compression — using visual tokens as a compressed, fixed-size representation of text-rich documents — implemented via a novel DeepEncoder architecture (serial SAM-base window attention → 16× convolutional compression → CLIP-large global attention) paired with a DeepSeek3B-MoE-A570M decoder.

papers.title: Higher-order Linear Attention
papers.pitch: Introduces Higher-order Linear Attention (HLA), a causal, streaming attention-like mechanism that realizes exact higher-order (second- and third-order) interactions via compact prefix sufficient statistics, enabling per-token O(1) state updates and linear-time inference without forming n×n affinity matrices. This makes attention-style, data-dependent mixing scalable and strictly autoregressive for

papers.title: SSA: Sparse Sparse Attention by Aligning Full and Sparse Attention Outputs in Feature Space
papers.pitch: This paper introduces SSA (Sparse Sparse Attention), a training framework that integrates both sparse and full attention within a single model by alternating between attention modes with equal probability and applying bidirectional alignment to encourage inherently sparser attention distributions.

papers.title: FASA: Frequency-aware Sparse Attention
papers.pitch: This paper introduces FASA (Frequency-Aware Sparse Attention), a training-free framework for query-aware token eviction during LLM decoding, evaluated across Llama, Mistral, and Qwen model families on LongBench, long-sequence modeling (PG-19, WikiText, C4), and long chain-of-thought reasoning (MATH500, AIME24).

papers.title: A Comprehensive Survey on Long Context Language Modeling
papers.pitch: This comprehensive survey unifies the fast-evolving domain of long-context language modeling (LCLM), detailing advances in data strategies, architectural innovations, workflow designs, infrastructure, evaluation, and applications for models that process hundreds of thousands to millions of tokens. Its core contribution is a holistic taxonomy and deep analysis of not only how to build and evaluate

papers.title: A Controlled Study on Long Context Extension and Generalization in LLMs
papers.pitch: This paper provides the first apples-to-apples comparison of methods for extending large language models (LLMs) to much longer input lengths by fixing a base model, dataset, and evaluation protocol. The study reveals that exact-attention, fine-tuned approaches—especially Dynamic NTK—best preserve accuracy for long-context tasks, while approximate-attention methods consistently underperform, and ge

papers.title: A Survey of Context Engineering for Large Language Models
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Context Engineering as a unified, formal discipline for systematically designing, optimizing, and integrating all facets of contextual information in Large Language Models (LLMs)—from retrieval and processing to dynamic assembly and system-level implementation. By synthesizing over 1,400 works, it builds the first comprehensive, end-to-end taxonomy that covers foundational te

papers.title: Deep contextualized word representations
papers.pitch: This paper introduces ELMo: deep contextualized word representations that generate word embeddings as a function of the entire input sentence by leveraging all layers of a large bidirectional language model (biLM). This innovation not only models complex, context-sensitive aspects of word meaning—including polysemy and syntax—but also delivers substantial improvements across a wide range of NLP ta

papers.title: LLM2Vec: Large Language Models Are Secretly Powerful Text Encoders
papers.pitch: LLM2Vec introduces a simple, unsupervised method that transforms any decoder-only large language model (LLM) into a high-performing universal text encoder using three lightweight steps: enabling bidirectional attention, masked next-token prediction, and unsupervised contrastive learning. This approach not only outperforms traditional encoder-only models on major text embedding benchmarks but also

papers.title: LLaVA-o1: Let Vision Language Models Reason Step-by-Step
papers.pitch: LLaVA-CoT introduces a novel, stage-structured approach for vision-language models, breaking reasoning down into explicit Summary, Caption, Reasoning, and Conclusion stages with self-aware transitions. This systematic pipeline, reinforced by a new 100k-sample dataset and a stage-wise retracing test-time search, dramatically boosts multimodal reasoning accuracy—outperforming even much larger or clo
papers.similarPaper: LLaVA-CoT: Let Vision Language Models Reason Step-by-Step
papers.scoreReason: The candidate paper and the history paper address the identical core problem of enabling step-by-step structured reasoning in Vision-Language Models, sharing the exact same subtitle and focusing on VLM reasoning enhancement.

papers.title: LongCodeZip: Compress Long Context for Code Language Models
papers.pitch: LongCodeZip introduces the first training-free, model-agnostic compression framework tailored for code LLMs handling extremely long contexts. By combining conditional perplexity-based mutual information scoring for function selection with fine-grained, knapsack-optimized block pruning, it aggressively reduces code context size—up to 5.6× compression—without degrading, and sometimes even improving,

papers.title: LongRoPE: Extending LLM Context Window Beyond 2 Million Tokens
papers.pitch: LongRoPE presents a breakthrough method to expand the usable context window of large language models from a mere few thousand to over two million tokens—more than 500× previous limits—without requiring massive retraining at ultra-long lengths. By intelligently learning dimension- and position-specific rescalings of rotary position embeddings, coupled with a progressive fine-tuning and interpolatio

papers.title: YARN: EFFICIENT CONTEXT WINDOW EXTENSION OF LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS
papers.pitch: YaRN introduces a breakthrough method for vastly extending the usable context window of transformer models using Rotary Position Embeddings, such as LLaMA and Mistral. By combining a targeted rescaling of positional frequencies with a simple attention scaling trick, YaRN enables models to handle ultra-long sequences (up to 128k tokens) with 10× less training data and 2.5× fewer steps than previous

papers.title: Realization of the anisotropic XY model in a Tb(III)-W(V) chain compound
papers.pitch: This paper presents experimental evidence that the cyanido-bridged chain compound [Tb(pzam)₃(H₂O)W(CN)₈]·H₂O realizes a one-dimensional S = 1/2 anisotropic XY ferromagnetic model in its paramagnetic phase, based on specific heat, susceptibility, and magnetization measurements on a powder sample.

papers.title: DeepWalk: Online Learning of Social Representations
papers.pitch: DeepWalk introduces a novel approach for learning latent representations of vertices in a network by repurposing neural language modeling techniques from sequences of words to graphs.

papers.title: Distributed Representations of Sentences and Documents
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Paragraph Vector, an unsupervised algorithm that learns fixed-length dense vector representations for variable-length pieces of text — sentences, paragraphs, and entire documents — by training a model to predict words in context using both word vectors and a document-level vector that acts as a memory of the paragraph's topic.

papers.title: LINE: Large-scale Information Network Embedding
papers.pitch: This paper proposes LINE (Large-scale Information Network Embedding), a novel graph embedding method that scales to networks with millions of vertices and billions of edges by optimizing carefully designed objective functions that preserve both first-order proximity (direct edge weights between vertices) and second-order proximity (similarity of neighborhood structures, capturing shared "conte

papers.title: Electronic structure of the high and low pressure polymorphs of MgSiN$_{2}$
papers.pitch: This paper analyzes the electronic structure and pressure-induced phase stability of the group II-IV nitride MgSiN₂ using density functional theory calculations across multiple exchange-correlation approximations—including the hybrid HSE06 functional—on the two known polymorphs of this material.

papers.title: Enriching Word Vectors with Subword Information
papers.pitch: This paper introduces an extension of the skipgram model that incorporates subword information by representing each word as the sum of vector representations of its character n-grams — a bag-of-characters approach that requires no morphological segmentation or supervision.

papers.title: SWAG: A Large-Scale Adversarial Dataset for Grounded Commonsense Inference
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the task of grounded commonsense inference and presents Swag (Situations With Adversarial Generations), a new dataset of 113k multiple-choice questions derived from pairs of temporally adjacent video captions, requiring models to select the most plausible next event given a partial description.

papers.title: The Pile: An 800GB Dataset of Diverse Text for Language Modeling
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the Pile, an 825 GiB English text corpus constructed from 22 diverse, high-quality datasets—spanning academic writing, code, legal opinions, and dialogue—targeted at training large-scale language models.

papers.title: The Flan Collection: Designing Data and Methods for Effective Instruction Tuning
papers.pitch: This paper studies the design decisions behind effective instruction tuning, using the Flan Collection of tasks and methods developed for the Flan 2022 models (Chung et al., 2022) and evaluated primarily on T5-XL (3B) models against benchmarks including MMLU and BIG-Bench Hard.

papers.title: Enhancing Chat Language Models by Scaling High-quality Instructional Conversations
papers.pitch: This paper introduces UltraChat, a large-scale, systematically constructed dataset of 1.5 million high-quality multi-turn instructional dialogues designed to cover the breadth of human-AI assistant interactions across three sectors—information access ("Questions about the World"), conditional information creation ("Creation and Generation"), and information transformation ("Assistance on Exist

papers.title: The RefinedWeb Dataset for Falcon LLM: Outperforming Curated Corpora with Web Data, and Web Data Only
papers.pitch: This paper introduces REFINEDWEB, a five-trillion-token English pretraining dataset built entirely from CommonCrawl web data through a novel pipeline called Macrodata Refinement (MDR) — combining stringent document-wise and line-wise filtering heuristics with aggressive deduplication (both fuzzy MinHash and exact substring removal, achieving ~50% removal rates) — and demonstrates, through

papers.title: MathPile: A Billion-Token-Scale Pretraining Corpus for Math
papers.pitch: This paper introduces MATHPILE, a diverse and high-quality math-centric pre-training corpus comprising approximately 9.5 billion tokens sourced from textbooks, arXiv papers, Wikipedia, ProofWiki, StackExchange, and Common Crawl, constructed under a "less is more" principle that prioritizes data quality over quantity.

papers.title: Cosmos World Foundation Model Platform for Physical AI
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the Cosmos World Foundation Model Platform, a comprehensive system for building and customizing world foundation models (WFMs)—digital twins of the physical world that Physical AI systems can safely interact with for policy evaluation, planning, and synthetic data generation.

papers.title: Towards Best Practices for Open Datasets for LLM Training
papers.pitch: This convening paper synthesizes expert consensus into concrete principles and technical best practices for building openly licensed, reproducible LLM training datasets—covering sourcing, metadata, preference signaling, processing, governance, and release. By addressing legal, technical, and sociological barriers (especially metadata gaps and opt-out mechanisms), it provides a practical roadmap to

papers.title: Fine-tuning Small Language Models as Efficient Enterprise Search Relevance Labelers
papers.pitch: This paper introduces a synthetic data generation pipeline that leverages an LLM—specifically GPT-4o—to synthesize realistic enterprise queries from seed documents, applies BM25 to retrieve challenging negatives, and uses a teacher LLM to assign graded relevance labels, producing query–document–label triplets that are distilled into a fine-tuned small language model (SLM) for efficient relevan

papers.title: Scaling Search Relevance: Augmenting App Store Ranking with LLM-Generated Judgments
papers.pitch: This paper deploys and validates an LLM-as-a-Judge paradigm at industrial scale for app-store search ranking, systematically comparing pretrained and fine-tuned in-house language models to generate pointwise textual relevance labels that augment a multi-objective production ranker.

papers.title: Accelerating t-SNE using Tree-Based Algorithms
papers.pitch: This paper develops two tree-based accelerations for t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE)—the Barnes-Hut approximation (replacing point-point repulsive forces with point-cell summaries evaluated via a quadtree depth-first search) and the dual-tree approximation (replacing them with cell-cell interactions via simultaneous dual quadtree traversal)—that reduce both gradient com

papers.title: Distributed Representations of Sentences and Documents
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Paragraph Vector, an unsupervised algorithm that learns fixed-length dense vector representations from variable-length pieces of text — sentences, paragraphs, or entire documents — by training each paragraph vector to contribute to predicting the surrounding words in contexts sampled from that paragraph.

papers.title: Regularization and Variable Selection via the Elastic Net
papers.pitch: This paper proposes the elastic net, a new regularization and variable selection method for linear regression that generalizes the lasso by combining L1 and L2 penalties to produce sparse models while encouraging a grouping effect — the tendency for strongly correlated predictors to enter or leave the model together.

papers.title: Mining Frequent Patterns without Candidate Generation
papers.pitch: This paper proposes a novel data structure—the frequent pattern tree (FP-tree) —and an associated mining algorithm, FP-growth, for discovering the complete set of frequent patterns in transaction databases without generating candidate itemsets.

papers.title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation
papers.pitch: This paper introduces GloVe (Global Vectors), a new global log-bilinear regression model that learns vector-space word representations by directly factorizing the logarithm of a word-word co-occurrence matrix with a novel weighted least-squares objective—combining the global statistical efficiency of matrix factorization with the meaningful linear substructures characteristic of local context-

papers.title: Hierarchical Dirichlet Processes
papers.pitch: This paper proposes the hierarchical Dirichlet process (HDP), a nonparametric Bayesian framework for clustering problems involving multiple groups of data that must share mixture components.

papers.title: A Global Geometric Framework for Nonlinear Dimensionality Reduction
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Isomap, a global geometric framework for nonlinear dimensionality reduction that combines the computational efficiency and global optimality guarantees of classical PCA and MDS with the flexibility to learn a broad class of nonlinear manifolds.

papers.title: Kernel Methods in Machine Learning
papers.pitch: This paper reviews and unifies a broad class of machine learning methods that formulate learning and estimation problems in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS).

papers.title: Latent Dirichlet Allocation
papers.pitch: This paper introduces latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA), a generative probabilistic model for collections of discrete data—most prominently text corpora—that represents documents as random mixtures over latent topics, where each topic is characterized by a distribution over words (a three-level hierarchical Bayesian model that treats both words and documents as exchangeable).

papers.title: Nonlinear Dimensionality Reduction by Locally Linear Embedding
papers.pitch: This paper introduces locally linear embedding (LLE), an unsupervised learning algorithm that computes low-dimensional, neighborhood-preserving embeddings of high-dimensional data by exploiting local linear reconstructions.

papers.title: Distance Metric Learning, with Application to Clustering with Side-Information
papers.pitch: This paper introduces an algorithm that learns a Mahalanobis distance metric over ℝⁿ from user-provided examples of similar (and optionally dissimilar) pairs of points, framing metric learning as a convex optimization problem that admits efficient, local-optima-free solutions.

papers.title: Matrix Factorization Techniques for Recommender Systems
papers.pitch: This blog post introduces a practical, incremental algorithm for matrix factorization—approximating a large sparse ratings matrix via a singular value decomposition (SVD) that is trained with gradient descent only on observed entries, treating the model as a sum of learned user-feature and movie-feature pairings (each representing a latent "aspect" like action affinity or comedy preference).

papers.title: Probabilistic Matrix Factorization
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Probabilistic Matrix Factorization (PMF), a probabilistic linear factor model for collaborative filtering that scales linearly with the number of observations.

papers.title: Random projection in dimensionality reduction: Applications to image and text data
papers.pitch: This paper studies random projection as a dimensionality reduction method for high-dimensional real-world data, presenting empirical results on both image data (1000 windows from 13 monochrome natural-scene images, 2500 dimensions) and text document data (2262 newsgroup documents across a 5000-term vocabulary).

papers.title: On Spectral Clustering: Analysis and an algorithm
papers.pitch: This paper analyzes a spectral clustering algorithm—a method that clusters points using eigenvectors of matrices derived from pairwise distances—and provides the first rigorous perturbation-theoretic conditions under which such an algorithm can be guaranteed to recover the correct clustering.

papers.title: Support Vector Clustering
papers.pitch: This paper introduces a novel clustering method, Support Vector Clustering (SVC), that repurposes the support vector formalism — originally developed for supervised classification — into an unsupervised algorithm by mapping data points via a Gaussian kernel to a high-dimensional feature space, finding the minimal enclosing sphere there, and interpreting the sphere's contours when mapped back t

papers.title: Visualizing Data using t-SNE
papers.pitch: This paper introduces t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE), a new technique for visualizing high-dimensional data in two or three dimensions by converting pairwise distances into joint probabilities and minimizing the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the high- and low-dimensional probability distributions. t-SNE modifies Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (SNE) through two key

papers.title: Fractional Helmholtz and fractional wave equations with Riesz-Feller and generalized Riemann-Liouville fractional derivatives
papers.pitch: This paper derives analytical solutions to fractional-order generalizations of the Laplace, Poisson, and Helmholtz equations in two variables, obtained by replacing integer-order partial derivatives with the Riesz-Feller fractional derivative (a pseudo-differential operator whose symbol is the logarithm of a Lévy stable distribution's characteristic function) and the Hilfer-composite fractio

papers.title: Conditional Generative Adversarial Nets
papers.pitch: This paper introduces conditional generative adversarial nets, a straightforward extension of the original GAN framework in which both the generator and discriminator receive auxiliary information `y` (class labels, tags, or data from other modalities) as additional input, enabling directed data generation rather than uncontrolled sampling from the model's learned distribution.

papers.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
papers.pitch: This paper introduces diffusion probabilistic models as a practical generative modeling framework capable of high-quality image synthesis, establishing that these models — previously known but not demonstrated at scale — can achieve sample quality rivaling or surpassing GANs.

papers.title: Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models
papers.pitch: This paper introduces denoising diffusion implicit models (DDIMs), a class of iterative implicit probabilistic models that accelerate sampling from denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) without changing the training procedure.

papers.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
