This empowers users with deep, auditable control over tool usage, process logic, and report structure, breaking the traditional lock-in of research agents to fixe

papers.title: Bigtable: A Distributed Storage System for Structured Data
papers.pitch: Bigtable introduces a distributed storage system for structured data designed to scale to petabytes across thousands of commodity servers, providing a simple data model that gives clients dynamic control over data layout and format.

papers.title: PyTorch: An Imperative Style, High-Performance Deep Learning Library
papers.pitch: PyTorch introduces an imperative-style deep learning library that demonstrates that usability and high performance are compatible goals within a single framework, eschewing the static dataflow graph paradigm of prior frameworks in favor of immediate execution of dynamic tensor computations.

papers.title: TensorFlow: A System for Large-Scale Machine Learning
papers.pitch: TensorFlow is a machine learning system that operates at large scale and in heterogeneous environments, using a unified dataflow graph to represent both computation and mutable state.

papers.title: BinaryConnect: Training Deep Neural Networks with binary weights during propagations
papers.pitch: This paper introduces BinaryConnect, a method for training deep neural networks where weights are constrained to exactly two values (+1 or −1) during the forward and backward propagations, while a full-precision real-valued weight is maintained for accumulating stochastic gradient updates.

papers.title: Binarized Neural Networks: Training Deep Neural Networks with Weights and Activations Constrained to +1 or -1
papers.pitch: This paper introduces a method to train Binarized Neural Networks (BNNs) — neural networks with both weights and activations constrained to +1 or −1 during the forward pass — and validates it on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and SVHN using MLP and ConvNet architectures in both Torch7 and Theano.

papers.title: XNOR-Net: ImageNet Classification Using Binary Convolutional Neural Networks
papers.pitch: This paper introduces two efficient approximations to standard convolutional neural networks: Binary-Weight-Networks and XNOR-Networks.

papers.title: Mixed Precision Training
papers.pitch: This paper introduces mixed precision training, a methodology that trains deep neural networks using IEEE half-precision (FP16) floating point numbers while matching the accuracy of single-precision (FP32) training without modifying model architectures or hyperparameters.

papers.title: Quantization and Training of Neural Networks for Efficient Integer-Arithmetic-Only Inference
papers.pitch: This paper proposes a quantization scheme that enables inference using integer-arithmetic-only computation — mapping weights and activations to 8-bit integers with an affine transformation — paired with a quantized training framework (injecting simulated quantization nodes into the forward pass while keeping weights in floating point) that preserves model accuracy post-quantization.

papers.title: Quantizing deep convolutional networks for efficient inference: A whitepaper
papers.pitch: This whitepaper surveys and empirically evaluates techniques for quantizing deep convolutional neural networks to 8-bit integer weights and activations for efficient inference on edge devices, studying tradeoffs across a range of architectures—MobileNets, ResNets, Inception-v3, and NasNet—on the ImageNet classification benchmark.

papers.title: HAWQ: Hessian AWare Quantization of Neural Networks with Mixed-Precision
papers.pitch: HAWQ introduces Hessian AWare Quantization, a second-order method that automatically selects the relative mixed-precision quantization configuration of each layer and determines a deterministic block-wise fine-tuning order — both based on the layer's Hessian spectrum (specifically, sorting by the top eigenvalue normalized by layer size for precision, and by eigenvalue times quantization pertur

papers.title: Q-BERT: Hessian Based Ultra Low Precision Quantization of BERT
papers.pitch: This paper proposes Q-BERT, a method for quantizing fine-tuned BERT models to ultra-low precision by performing an extensive second-order Hessian analysis of each encoder layer to guide mixed-precision bit assignment and by introducing a new group-wise quantization scheme (partitioning each matrix into groups with independent quantization ranges and lookup tables).

papers.title: Q8BERT: Quantized 8Bit BERT
papers.pitch: This paper introduces a method for compressing BERT through quantization-aware training during fine-tuning, quantizing all General Matrix Multiply (GEMM) operations in the Fully Connected and Embedding layers to 8-bit integers — achieving a 4× reduction in memory footprint with minimal accuracy loss.

papers.title: BinaryBERT: Pushing the Limit of BERT Quantization
papers.pitch: This paper proposes BinaryBERT, a method that pushes BERT quantization to the limit by binarizing weights to 1-bit.

papers.title: ZeroQuant: Efficient and Affordable Post-Training Quantization for Large-Scale Transformers
papers.pitch: This paper introduces ZeroQuant, an end-to-end post-training quantization and inference pipeline that compresses large Transformer-based language models without requiring retraining or access to original training data.

papers.title: LLM.int8(): 8-bit Matrix Multiplication for Transformers at Scale
papers.pitch: The paper introduces LLM.int8(), a post-training method combining vector-wise Int8 quantization with a mixed-precision decomposition that isolates rare high-magnitude hidden-feature outliers into 16-bit operations, enabling nearly all matrix multiplications in transformers to run in 8-bit without accuracy loss. By cutting weight memory roughly in half (e.g., ~1.96× for BLOOM-176B) and preserving f

papers.title: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers
papers.pitch: This paper introduces GPTQ, a new one-shot post-training weight quantization method based on approximate second-order information that is both highly-accurate and highly-efficient for compressing Generative Pre-trained Transformer models such as OPT and BLOOM.

papers.title: SmoothQuant: Accurate and Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Large Language Models
papers.pitch: This paper proposes SmoothQuant, a training-free post-training quantization method that enables 8-bit weight and 8-bit activation (W8A8) quantization for large language models without accuracy degradation.

papers.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
papers.pitch: This paper introduces QLORA, an efficient finetuning method that reduces memory usage enough to finetune a 65B parameter model on a single 48GB GPU while preserving full 16-bit finetuning task performance.

papers.title: Training Transformers with 4-bit Integers
papers.pitch: This paper proposes a hardware-friendly INT4 training algorithm for transformers that implements all matrix multiplications with 4-bit integer arithmetic, addressing a gap in prior 4-bit training methods that require custom numerical formats unsupported by contemporary GPUs.

papers.title: Quantizable Transformers: Removing Outliers by Helping Attention Heads Do Nothing
papers.pitch: This paper analyzes the root cause of activation outliers that make transformers difficult to quantize, establishing that these outliers arise because attention heads learn a "no-op" behavior—attempting to avoid updating the residual stream by allocating nearly all attention probability to low-information tokens (e.g., delimiter tokens like `[SEP]` in BERT or background patches in ViT), which

papers.title: FLIQS: One-Shot Mixed-Precision Floating-Point and Integer Quantization Search
papers.pitch: This paper introduces FLIQS (Floating-Point and Integer Quantization Search), the first one-shot mixed-precision quantization search framework that eliminates the need for post-search retraining by employing a cosine entropy regularization schedule that gradually reduces policy exploration during training.

papers.title: OmniQuant: Omnidirectionally Calibrated Quantization for Large Language Models
papers.pitch: This paper introduces OmniQuant, a differentiable post-training quantization technique for large language models that achieves quantization-aware training (QAT)-level performance while maintaining the time and data efficiency of PTQ methods.

papers.title: Efficient Post-training Quantization with FP8 Formats
papers.pitch: This paper studies the advantages of FP8 floating-point formats for post-training quantization across 75 unique network architectures and 200+ tasks spanning NLP, computer vision, speech, and recommendation.

papers.title: LoftQ: LoRA-Fine-Tuning-Aware Quantization for Large Language Models
papers.pitch: This paper introduces LoftQ (LoRA-Fine-Tuning-Aware Quantization), a quantization framework that jointly optimizes the quantized backbone and low-rank adapter initialization for LLMs prior to LoRA fine-tuning, rather than quantizing the pre-trained weights independently and initializing adapters to zero as in QLoRA.

papers.title: Microscaling Data Formats for Deep Learning
papers.pitch: This paper evaluates Microscaling (MX) data formats — a family of narrow bit-width datatypes that combine a per-block scaling factor with low-precision floating-point and integer elements — as a drop-in replacement for FP32 across over two dozen deep learning benchmarks, including GPT-3-175B, LLaMA-7B, and GPT-like models up to 1.5B parameters.

papers.title: BitNet: Scaling 1-bit Transformers for Large Language Models
papers.pitch: This paper introduces BitNet, a 1-bit Transformer architecture that replaces standard matrix multiplication with a binarized linear layer called BitLinear (using the signum function to constrain weights to +1 or −1 paired with absmax activation quantization).

papers.title: QMoE: Practical Sub-1-Bit Compression of Trillion-Parameter Models
papers.pitch: This paper introduces QMoE, a compression and execution framework that accurately compresses trillion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts models to less than 1 bit per parameter through a co-designed system of scalable data-dependent quantization and a custom entropy-aware encoding scheme paired with bespoke GPU decoding kernels.

papers.title: LLM-FP4: 4-Bit Floating-Point Quantized Transformers
papers.pitch: This paper proposes LLM-FP4, a post-training quantization method that compresses both weights and activations in transformer models to 4-bit floating-point values.

papers.title: Atom: Low-bit Quantization for Efficient and Accurate LLM Serving
papers.pitch: Atom introduces a low-bit weight-activation quantization method for LLM serving that combines mixed-precision quantization (keeping 128 outlier channels in INT8 while quantizing remaining values to INT4), fine-grained group quantization (dividing matrices into subgroups of 128 elements with fused dequantization in the GEMM pipeline), and dynamic activation quantization (computing quant

papers.title: ZeroQuant(4+2): Redefining LLMs Quantization with a New FP6-Centric Strategy for Diverse Generative Tasks
papers.pitch: This paper studies how to improve weight-only quantization for LLMs on generative tasks by shifting from INT4 to FP6 precision, analyzing the limitations of INT4 across zero-shot evaluation, code generation, and abstractive summarization benchmarks using LLaMA (1B–65B), StarCoder-15B, CodeGeeX2-6B, and BART-406M models.

papers.title: QuaRot: Outlier-Free 4-Bit Inference in Rotated LLMs
papers.pitch: This paper introduces QuaRot, a quantization scheme that applies randomized Hadamard rotations to eliminate outlier features from LLM hidden states without altering model output, enabling end-to-end 4-bit quantization of all weights, activations, and KV caches.

papers.title: Spectra: Surprising Effectiveness of Pretraining Ternary Language Models at Scale
papers.pitch: This paper introduces and systematically evaluates Ternary Language Models (TriLMs) — models whose linear layer weights are constrained to the set {−1, 0, +1} during training via on-the-fly ternarization with a learned per-matrix scale — as an alternative to both standard floating-point models (FloatLMs) and post-training quantized models (QuantLMs) for addressing the memory-capacity and memor

papers.title: VPTQ: Extreme Low-bit Vector Post-Training Quantization for Large Language Models
papers.pitch: VPTQ introduces Vector Post-Training Quantization, an extreme low-bit weight-only quantization method for LLMs that uses vector quantization to compress weight matrices into indices referencing learned codebooks.

papers.title: PrefixQuant: Eliminating Outliers by Prefixed Tokens for Large Language Models Quantization
papers.pitch: PrefixQuant proposes a novel quantization method that isolates token-wise outliers — activation values orders of magnitude larger than normal tokens that cause disproportionate quantization error — by prefixing high-frequency outlier tokens (e.g., `. \n` for Llama-2-7B) directly into the KV cache, a training-free process that completes in under one minute for Llama-3-70B.

papers.title: BitNet a4.8: 4-bit Activations for 1-bit LLMs
papers.pitch: BitNet a4.8 introduces a hybrid quantization and sparsification strategy that enables 4-bit activations for 1-bit LLMs (specifically, models with ternary weights at {-1, 0, 1} as in BitNet b1.58), selectively applying 4-bit quantization to Gaussian-like attention and FFN inputs while using Top-K sparsification with 8-bit retention for outlier-heavy intermediate states.

papers.title: Cut Your Losses in Large-Vocabulary Language Models
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Cut Cross-Entropy (CCE), a method that computes the cross-entropy loss and its gradient without materializing the full logit matrix — entries for every token-vocabulary pair — in global GPU memory, instead computing logits on the fly in on-chip SRAM and evaluating the log-sum-exp reduction incrementally.

papers.title: Optimizing Large Language Model Training Using FP4 Quantization
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the first FP4 training framework for large language models, addressing the significant quantization errors and limited representational capacity that make 4-bit training challenging.

papers.title: Matryoshka Quantization
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Matryoshka Quantization (MatQuant), a multi-scale training technique that jointly optimizes a single model across multiple integer precision levels—int8, int4, and int2—by leveraging the nested (Matryoshka) structure of integer data types, where smaller bit-widths are contained within the most significant bits of larger ones (slicing an int8 model's MSBs directly yields i

papers.title: SageAttention2++: A More Efficient Implementation of SageAttention2
papers.pitch: SageAttention2++ proposes a more efficient implementation of the SageAttention2 attention quantization method by leveraging a faster GPU instruction—`mma.f16.f8.f8.f16`, which performs FP8 matrix multiplication with an FP16 accumulator and is 4× faster than FP16—for the PV matrix multiplication in attention, replacing the slower `mma.f32.f8.f8.f32` instruction used in SageAttention2.

papers.title: The Geometry of LLM Quantization: GPTQ as Babai's Nearest Plane Algorithm
papers.pitch: This paper reveals that GPTQ—a standard one-shot post-training quantization method for large language models—is mathematically identical to Babai’s nearest plane algorithm for the classical closest vector problem (CVP) on a lattice defined by the layer’s input Hessian, provided GPTQ executes back-to-front (from last to first dimension) without weight clipping.

papers.title: Bridging the Gap Between Promise and Performance for Microscaling FP4 Quantization
papers.pitch: This paper provides the first comprehensive empirical study of the recently hardware-accelerated MXFP4 and NVFP4 microscaling 4-bit floating-point formats for post-training quantization of LLMs, revealing that state-of-the-art PTQ methods struggle with FP4 due to NVFP4's small group size neutralizing outlier mitigation and MXFP4's power-of-two scale quantization inducing severe accuracy degradatio

papers.title: INT v.s. FP: A Comprehensive Study of Fine-Grained Low-bit Quantization Formats
papers.pitch: This paper delivers a unified, theoretical and empirical comparison of fine-grained low-bit integer (INT) vs. floating-point (FP) quantization across block-wise formats (MX, NV), revealing a crossover: while FP wins at coarse granularity, MXINT8 often outperforms MXFP8 in both accuracy and hardware efficiency at block sizes used in practice. Four Over Six: More Accurate NVFP4 Quantization with Adaptive Block Scaling
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Four Over Six (4/6), a modification to the NVFP4 block-scaled quantization algorithm that improves numerical accuracy by adaptively scaling some blocks to a maximum FP4 value of 4 rather than the standard 6, yielding reduced quantization error for near-maximal values that are otherwise unrepresentable in the 66.6%–100% range of a block's largest magnitude.

papers.title: Stronger Normalization-Free Transformers
papers.pitch: The paper introduces Dynamic erf (Derf), a simple learnable point-wise replacement for normalization layers defined as Derf(x)=γ·erf(αx+s)+β, found via a principled search over function properties. papers.title: Quartet II: Accurate LLM Pre-Training in NVFP4 by Improved Unbiased Gradient Estimation
papers.pitch: This paper proposes Quartet II, a fully-NVFP4 computation scheme for LLM pre-training that improves gradient estimation by replacing element-wise stochastic rounding (SR) with a novel unbiased quantization primitive called MS-EDEN (MicroScaling EDEN), which shifts stochasticity from individual FP4 values to the microscale factors while retaining unbiasedness in expectation and achieving mo

papers.title: AWQ: Activation-Aware Weight Quantization for On-Device LLM Compression and Acceleration
papers.pitch: AWQ introduces a novel, hardware-friendly quantization method that compresses large language models to 4-bit weights by using activation statistics to identify and protect a tiny subset of essential weights via per-channel scaling—delivering minimal accuracy loss. Coupled with the TinyChat inference system, this approach enables 3×–4× real-world speedups and democratizes state-of-the-art LLM and m

papers.title: FP8-LM: Training FP8 Large Language Models
papers.pitch: This paper presents FP8-LM, the first end-to-end framework for training large language models (LLMs) entirely in 8-bit floating point precision—not just compute, but also optimizer states and inter-GPU communication. By innovatively addressing the numerical instabilities of FP8, this approach delivers up to 39% lower memory usage and 75% faster training versus standard BF16 methods, all while pres

papers.title: Pretraining Large Language Models with NVFP4
papers.pitch: This paper presents the first stable and accurate methodology for pretraining large language models with 4-bit floating point (FP4) precision using the new NVFP4 format—integrating innovations such as 2D weight scaling, Random Hadamard transforms, stochastic rounding on gradients, and selective high-precision layers. The approach is validated at unprecedented scale (training a 12B-parameter model

papers.title: SageAttention3: Microscaling FP4 Attention for Inference and An Exploration of 8-Bit Training
papers.pitch: SageAttention3 introduces the first practical 4-bit (FP4) 'microscaling' attention kernel for GPU inference, leveraging new Blackwell FP4 Tensor Cores to achieve up to 5× faster performance than state-of-the-art methods—while maintaining model accuracy in demanding text, image, and video generation tasks. papers.pitch: This paper introduces BitNet b1.58, a Transformer-based large language model where every weight is constrained to the ternary set {−1, 0, +1}, achieving state-of-the-art language modeling performance at just 1.58 bits per weight. papers.title: Learning Factored Representations in a Deep Mixture of Experts
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the Deep Mixture of Experts (DMoE), a stacked extension of the standard Mixture of Experts that places separate gating networks at each layer, enabling an exponentially large number of effective expert combinations — each input dynamically assembles a different path through the network (e.g., one first-layer expert specializing in digit location and one second-layer exper

papers.title: GShard: Scaling Giant Models with Conditional Computation and Automatic Sharding
papers.pitch: This paper introduces GShard, a module consisting of lightweight annotation APIs and an XLA compiler extension that automatically partitions neural network computation across thousands of devices while keeping compilation time constant.

papers.title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the Switch Transformer, a sparsely-activated expert architecture that simplifies Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) routing by selecting only a single expert per token rather than the top-k (where k > 1), while introducing training techniques — selective precision casting of router operations to float32 within bfloat16 training and reduced parameter initialization scale — that stab

papers.title: GLaM: Efficient Scaling of Language Models with Mixture-of-Experts
papers.pitch: This paper introduces and evaluates GLaM (Generalist Language Model), a family of decoder-only language models that uses a sparsely activated mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture to scale model capacity while constraining computational cost.

papers.title: ST-MoE: Designing Stable and Transferable Sparse Expert Models
papers.pitch: This paper systematically studies how to improve the training stability, fine-tuning transfer performance, and architectural design of sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models, validated on a 269B-parameter encoder-decoder model (ST-MoE-32B) evaluated across SuperGLUE, ARC, summarization benchmarks, and closed-book QA tasks.

papers.title: Tutel: Adaptive Mixture-of-Experts at Scale
papers.pitch: This paper introduces TUTEL, a full-stack system design and implementation that optimizes sparsely-gated mixture-of-experts (MoE) layers by adapting to their inherently dynamic workload at runtime.

papers.title: RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the Receptance Weighted Key Value (RWKV) model architecture, which reformulates the Transformer attention mechanism into a linear variant—combining parallelizable training with recurrent-style inference—to eliminate the quadratic memory and computational scaling of standard self-attention.

papers.title: From Sparse to Soft Mixtures of Experts
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Soft MoE, a fully-differentiable sparse Transformer layer that replaces the discrete token-to-expert assignment problem of conventional Sparse MoEs with an implicit soft assignment—each expert processes a learned convex combination of all input tokens rather than a hard subset of them.

papers.title: Memory Augmented Language Models through Mixture of Word Experts
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Mixture of Word Experts (MoWE), a sparse Transformer architecture that decouples learning capacity from compute by replacing standard feed-forward layers with a massively expanded pool of word-specific experts—tens of thousands of small MLPs, each activated by a fixed routing function tied to a knowledge-rich auxiliary vocabulary.

papers.title: SwitchHead: Accelerating Transformers with Mixture-of-Experts Attention
papers.pitch: This paper introduces SwitchHead, a novel Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) method for the self-attention layer of Transformers that reduces both compute and memory requirements while matching the language modeling performance of parameter-matched dense baselines.

papers.title: MoE-Mamba: Efficient Selective State Space Models with Mixture of Experts
papers.pitch: This paper proposes that State Space Models can be scaled more efficiently by combining them with Mixture of Experts, and introduces MoE-Mamba, a model that interleaves Mamba layers with Switch Transformer MoE feed-forward layers to separate unconditional sequence processing from conditional per-token expert computation.

papers.title: Branch-Train-MiX: Mixing Expert LLMs into a Mixture-of-Experts LLM
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Branch-Train-MiX (BTX), a continued pretraining method that improves a generalist LLM's capabilities across multiple specialized domains by first training domain experts in an embarrassingly parallel fashion from a shared seed model, then merging them into a single Mixture-of-Experts model with learned token-level routing.

papers.title: Mixture-of-Depths: Dynamically allocating compute in transformer-based language models
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Mixture-of-Depths (MoD), a conditional computation method for transformer-based language models that learns to dynamically allocate FLOPs across sequence positions and model depth by capping the number of tokens that participate in self-attention and MLP computations at a given layer — routing the remaining tokens through a cheap residual connection instead.

papers.title: JetMoE: Reaching Llama2 Performance with 0.1M Dollars
papers.pitch: This paper introduces JetMoE-8B, a new large language model that achieves performance competitive with Llama2-7B while being trained for under $0.1 million using only 1.25T tokens of public data and 30,000 H100 GPU hours.

papers.title: Layerwise Recurrent Router for Mixture-of-Experts
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the Layerwise Recurrent Router for Mixture-of-Experts (RMoE), a new routing mechanism that integrates a lightweight Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) across consecutive transformer layers to establish dependencies between routing decisions, replacing the standard practice where routers in different MoE layers operate independently without sharing historical assignment informatio

papers.title: MH-MoE: Multi-Head Mixture-of-Experts
papers.pitch: This paper introduces a novel implementation of Multi-Head Mixture-of-Experts (MH-MoE) that achieves FLOPs and parameter parity with standard sparse Mixture-of-Experts models, addressing the computational overhead present in the original MH-MoE formulation.

papers.title: SonicMoE: Accelerating MoE with IO and Tile-aware Optimizations

papers.title: Coupling Experts and Routers in Mixture-of-Experts via an Auxiliary Loss
papers.pitch: The paper introduces expert-router coupling (ERC) loss, a lightweight auxiliary loss that uses perturbed router embeddings as proxy tokens to probe all experts and enforce margin-style constraints so router embeddings and expert activations become mutually consistent. papers.title: Arcee Trinity Large Technical Report
papers.pitch: This technical report introduces the Trinity family of open-weight sparse Mixture-of-Experts language models—Trinity Nano (6B total, 1B activated), Trinity Mini (26B total, 3B activated), and Trinity Large (400B total, 13B activated)—trained on up to 17 trillion tokens using the Muon optimizer with zero loss spikes throughout.

papers.title: Show and Tell: A Neural Image Caption Generator
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Neural Image Caption (NIC), an end-to-end generative model that produces natural-language descriptions of images by combining a convolutional neural network image encoder with a Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) sentence decoder — directly maximizing the probability of the correct description given the image (p(S|I)).

papers.title: Show, Attend and Tell: Neural Image Caption Generation with Visual Attention
papers.pitch: This paper introduces an attention-based neural image caption generation model that learns to dynamically focus on salient regions of an image while generating each word of a descriptive sentence, evaluated on the Flickr8k, Flickr30k, and MS COCO benchmarks using a convolutional encoder (Oxford VGGnet) and an LSTM decoder.

papers.title: Bottom-Up and Top-Down Attention for Image Captioning and Visual Question Answering
papers.pitch: This paper proposes a combined bottom-up and top-down attention mechanism for image captioning and visual question answering, where bottom-up attention (a Faster R-CNN object detector that proposes salient image regions with associated feature vectors) supplies the spatial candidates over which top-down attention (task-specific context from a partially-generated caption or question representat

papers.title: Graph Attention Networks
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Graph Attention Networks (GATs), a novel graph neural architecture that uses masked self-attention to learn adaptive, per-neighbor weights during message passing. papers.title: ViLBERT: Pretraining Task-Agnostic Visiolinguistic Representations for Vision-and-Language Tasks
papers.pitch: This paper introduces ViLBERT (short for Vision-and-Language BERT), a model for learning task-agnostic joint representations of image content and natural language through pretraining on automatically collected image-caption data, then transferring to downstream vision-and-language tasks.

papers.title: VisualBERT: A Simple and Performant Baseline for Vision and Language
papers.pitch: This paper introduces VisualBERT, a simple framework for vision-and-language tasks that processes text tokens and image region features jointly through a single stack of Transformer layers, using self-attention to implicitly align words with visual elements.

papers.title: LXMERT: Learning Cross-Modality Encoder Representations from Transformers
papers.pitch: This paper introduces LXMERT (Learning Cross-Modality Encoder Representations from Transformers), a framework for learning joint vision-and-language representations through large-scale pre-training followed by task-specific fine-tuning.

papers.title: UNITER: UNiversal Image-TExt Representation Learning
papers.pitch: This paper introduces UNITER (UNiversal Image-TExt Representation), a large-scale pre-trained model that learns joint multimodal embeddings from four image-text datasets (COCO, Visual Genome, Conceptual Captions, and SBU Captions) using a single-stream Transformer architecture.

papers.title: Oscar: Object-Semantics Aligned Pre-training for Vision-Language Tasks
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Oscar (Object-Semantics Aligned Pre-training), a new vision-language pre-training method that uses object tags detected in images as anchor points to ease the learning of semantic alignments between image regions and text, motivated by the observation that salient objects in an image can be accurately detected and are often mentioned in the paired text.

papers.title: VinVL: Revisiting Visual Representations in Vision-Language Models
papers.pitch: This paper revisits and substantially improves the visual representations used in vision-language (VL) models by developing a new, larger object detection model that provides richer object-centric image features.

papers.title: ViLT: Vision-and-Language Transformer Without Convolution or Region Supervision
papers.pitch: This paper introduces ViLT (Vision-and-Language Transformer), a minimal VLP architecture that eliminates convolutional neural networks and region supervision from the visual embedding pipeline, instead processing image patches through a simple linear projection and delegating all visual feature extraction to a single unified transformer — a design it describes as "monolithic" in treating visua

papers.title: Scaling Up Visual and Vision-Language Representation Learning With Noisy Text Supervision

papers.pitch: This paper proposes DeBERTaV3, a new pre-trained language model that improves DeBERTa by replacing masked language modeling (MLM) with replaced token detection (RTD) — an ELECTRA-style pre-training task where a discriminator predicts whether each token is original or was replaced by a generator — and introduces Gradient-Disentangled Embedding Sharing (GDES) to resolve the "tug-of-war" dyna

papers.title: Grokking: Generalization Beyond Overfitting on Small Algorithmic Datasets
papers.pitch: This paper introduces and systematically studies “grokking,” a striking training dynamic on small, algorithmically generated binary-operation datasets where models first memorize the training set and only after vastly more optimization suddenly achieve perfect generalization. papers.title: UL2: Unifying Language Learning Paradigms
papers.pitch: This paper introduces UL2, a unified framework for pre-training language models that combines diverse self-supervision objectives into a single Mixture-of-Denoisers (MoD) — a blended objective comprising R-denoising (standard span corruption, as in T5), S-denoising (sequential prefix language modeling, akin to causal LMs), and X-denoising (extreme denoising with long spans and high corrupt

papers.title: In-context Learning and Induction Heads
papers.pitch: This paper identifies and characterizes “induction heads,” a specific attention-head circuit that appears during an early training “phase change” and provides strong evidence that these circuits are a primary mechanism for transformers’ in‑context learning. papers.title: Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision
papers.pitch: This paper studies the capabilities of speech recognition systems trained simply to predict large amounts of transcripts of audio on the internet, demonstrating that scaling weakly supervised pre-training to 680,000 hours of multilingual and multitask data produces models that generalize well to standard benchmarks in a zero-shot transfer setting without any fine-tuning.

papers.title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
papers.pitch: This paper introduces LLaMA, a collection of foundation language models ranging from 7B to 65B parameters trained exclusively on publicly available data.

papers.title: DoReMi: Optimizing Data Mixtures Speeds Up Language Model Pretraining
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Domain Reweighting with Minimax Optimization (DoReMi), an algorithm that uses a small proxy model (280M parameters) trained with Group DRO over domains to produce domain weights—sampling probabilities for each pretraining data domain—which then govern the training of a much larger model (8B parameters, a ~30× increase).

papers.title: The False Promise of Imitating Proprietary LLMs
papers.pitch: This paper critically analyzes the efficacy of model imitation—the practice of fine-tuning a weaker open-source language model on outputs from a stronger proprietary system like ChatGPT (e.g., Alpaca, Self-Instruct)—to cheaply close the capabilities gap.

papers.title: Binary and Ternary Natural Language Generation
papers.pitch: This paper introduces and empirically validates TBT (Ternary / Binary Transformer), a framework for quantizing both weights and activations of encoder-decoder transformer models to 2-bit ternary or 1-bit binary precision for natural language generation tasks.

papers.title: Orca: Progressive Learning from Complex Explanation Traces of GPT-4
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Explanation Tuning, a method for training smaller language models to imitate the reasoning process of large foundation models (LFMs) by augmenting standard ⟨query, response⟩ pairs with detailed step-by-step explanations, thought processes, and other complex instructions elicited from GPT-4 via curated system messages.

papers.title: Estimating the Causal Effect of Early ArXiving on Paper Acceptance
papers.pitch: This paper uses ICLR 2018–2022 observational data and a causal-inference pipeline—covariate matching combined with a negative-control outcome (long-term citation indicator) and difference-in-differences reasoning—to estimate the effect of posting a preprint before the review deadline on acceptance. papers.title: Emu: Generative Pretraining in Multimodality
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Emu, a multimodal foundation model that unifies image and text generation under a single autoregressive training objective—predicting the next element in multimodality—where the model learns to either classify the next text token or regress the next visual embedding in an interleaved multimodal sequence.

papers.title: When Less is More: Investigating Data Pruning for Pretraining LLMs at Scale
papers.pitch: This work systematically investigates data pruning for large language model pretraining—determining whether a subset of training data can match or exceed the performance of the full dataset—by comparing three automatic quality estimators on CommonCrawl-pretrained models up to 1.5B parameters.

papers.title: Effective Long-Context Scaling of Foundation Models
papers.pitch: This paper introduces a series of long-context LLMs built through continual pretraining from LLAMA 2, supporting effective context windows up to 32,768 tokens and demonstrating that long-context capability can be acquired efficiently without pretraining from scratch.

papers.title: Parameter-Efficient Orthogonal Finetuning via Butterfly Factorization
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Orthogonal Butterfly (BOFT), a parameter-efficient finetuning method that composes a dense orthogonal matrix as a product of multiple sparse orthogonal matrices structured according to butterfly factorization — inspired by the Cooley-Tukey fast Fourier transform algorithm — to adapt large foundation models while preserving pairwise neuron angles.

papers.title: Magicoder: Empowering Code Generation with OSS-Instruct
papers.pitch: This paper introduces OSS-INSTRUCT, a novel data generation method that leverages open-source code snippets as inspiration for a teacher LLM to automatically synthesize diverse, realistic programming problems and solutions, then uses this synthetic data to instruction-tune smaller code models.

papers.title: Long Context Compression with Activation Beacon
papers.pitch: This paper proposes Activation Beacon, a plug-in module for transformer-based LLMs that enables long context compression by distilling raw input into a small set of beacon tokens' activations (keys and values at every layer) through a progressive, fine-grained compression workflow where each chunk is interleaved with beacon tokens and encoded sequentially.

papers.title: Data Engineering for Scaling Language Models to 128K Context
papers.pitch: This paper studies how to scale an LLM's context length to 128K through lightweight continual pretraining, using LLaMA-2 7B and 13B as the base models evaluated primarily on the Needle-in-a-Haystack retrieval test.

papers.title: Simple and Scalable Strategies to Continually Pre-train Large Language Models
papers.pitch: This paper studies how to update large language models on new data without re-training from scratch, evaluating decoder-only transformers up to 10B parameters on the Pile→SlimPajama (weak shift) and Pile→German Common Crawl (stronger shift) pre-training distributions.

papers.title: The Unreasonable Ineffectiveness of the Deeper Layers
papers.pitch: This paper studies how knowledge is stored in LLM weights by analyzing the robustness of open-weight models to layer pruning—removing entire blocks of layers identified via angular distance similarity between representations—and then “healing” the damage with parameter-efficient finetuning (QLoRA).

papers.title: Rho-1: Not All Tokens Are What You Need
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Selective Language Modeling (SLM), a new pretraining objective that challenges the standard practice of applying a next-token prediction loss uniformly to all tokens.

papers.title: Replacing Judges with Juries: Evaluating LLM Generations with a Panel of Diverse Models
papers.pitch: This paper proposes evaluating LLM generations using a Panel of LLm evaluators (PoLL) — a diverse set of smaller models from different families whose judgments are pooled, rather than relying on a single large judge like GPT-4.

papers.title: Extending Llama-3's Context Ten-Fold Overnight
papers.pitch: This technical report proposes an efficient QLoRA fine-tuning recipe that extends the context length of Llama-3-8B-Instruct from 8K to 80K using merely 3.5K synthetic training samples generated by GPT-4, completing in 8 hours on a single 8×A800 machine.

papers.title: Samba: Simple Hybrid State Space Models for Efficient Unlimited Context Language Modeling
papers.pitch: This paper introduces SAMBA, a simple hybrid neural architecture that layer-wise interleaves Mamba—a selective State Space Model (SSM)—with Sliding Window Attention (SWA) and MLP layers to achieve efficient language modeling with unlimited context length extrapolation.

papers.title: How Do Large Language Models Acquire Factual Knowledge During Pretraining?
papers.pitch: This work studies the fine-grained dynamics of how large language models acquire factual knowledge during pretraining, using the OLMo model family with a constructed FICTIONAL KNOWLEDGE dataset of novel entity descriptions.

papers.title: Step-DPO: Step-wise Preference Optimization for Long-chain Reasoning of LLMs
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Step-DPO, a method that reformulates Direct Preference Optimization for long-chain mathematical reasoning by treating individual reasoning steps—rather than complete answers—as the fundamental units of preference comparison (maximizing the probability of a correct next step `swin` while minimizing an incorrect one `slose`, given the same preceding correct context).

papers.title: RegMix: Data Mixture as Regression for Language Model Pre-training
papers.pitch: This paper proposes REGMIX, a method that formulates data mixture selection for LLM pre-training as a regression task — training many small proxy models on diverse mixtures, fitting a regression model to predict unseen mixture performance, and applying the best predicted mixture to large-scale training.

papers.title: SAM 2: Segment Anything in Images and Videos
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM 2), a unified foundation model for promptable visual segmentation that extends the Segment Anything (SA) task from static images to videos.

papers.title: BaichuanSEED: Sharing the Potential of ExtensivE Data Collection and Deduplication by Introducing a Competitive Large Language Model Baseline
papers.pitch: This technical report introduces BaichuanSEED, a 7B-parameter large language model trained from scratch on 3T tokens to serve as a transparent, competitive baseline that explores the limits of model capability achievable through broad data collection and reweighting alone—deliberately avoiding fine-grained data selection, synthetic data, and downstream benchmark optimization.

papers.title: Scaling Smart: Accelerating Large Language Model Pre-training with Small Model Initialization
papers.pitch: This paper introduces HyperCloning, a method that initializes the parameters of a large language model by expanding the weights of a smaller pre-trained model, ensuring the larger model functionally preserves the smaller model's output logits before training begins.

papers.pitch: MaskLLM introduces learnable semi-structured sparsity for large language models, a pruning method that explicitly models N:M mask selection as a categorical distribution optimized via Gumbel Softmax sampling, enabling end-to-end training on large-scale datasets rather than relying on small calibration sets and handcrafted importance criteria.

papers.title: Byte Latent Transformer: Patches Scale Better Than Tokens
papers.pitch: The Byte Latent Transformer (BLT) introduces a tokenizer-free LLM architecture that learns directly from raw bytes and, for the first time, matches tokenization-based LLM performance at scale while improving inference efficiency and robustness.

papers.title: Leveraging Passage Retrieval with Generative Models for Open Domain Question Answering

papers.title: Unsupervised Dense Information Retrieval with Contrastive Learning

papers.title: Optimizing Test-Time Query Representations for Dense Retrieval

papers.title: BM25 Query Augmentation Learned End-to-End

papers.title: Democratizing Reasoning Ability: Tailored Learning from Large Language Model

papers.title: LiNR: Model Based Neural Retrieval on GPUs at LinkedIn

papers.title: Reusing Pre-Training Data at Test Time is a Compute Multiplier

papers.title: OpenAI Gym

papers.title: Rainbow: Combining Improvements in Deep Reinforcement Learning
papers.pitch: This paper empirically studies whether six independently developed extensions to the DQN algorithm—addressing overestimation bias, data efficiency, network architecture, multi-step targets, return distribution modeling, and exploration—are complementary and can be fruitfully combined into a single integrated agent.

papers.title: Mastering Chess and Shogi by Self-Play with a General Reinforcement Learning Algorithm

papers.title: Soft Actor-Critic Algorithms and Applications

papers.title: Conservative Q-Learning for Offline Reinforcement Learning

papers.title: Contrastive Preference Learning: Learning from Human Feedback without RL

papers.title: ODIN: Disentangled Reward Mitigates Hacking in RLHF

papers.pitch: This note analyzes the mathematical relationship between GloVe (Global Vectors for word representation) and SGNS (skip-gram with negative-sampling, implemented in word2vec), demonstrating that the two models — despite defining their cost functions differently — share fundamentally similar training objectives.

papers.title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Batch Normalization, a mechanism for accelerating deep neural network training by reducing what the authors term Internal Covariate Shift — the change in the distribution of each layer's inputs as preceding layer parameters update during training.

papers.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
papers.pitch: This paper introduces distillation, a method for transferring the knowledge from a cumbersome model—an ensemble or a single large regularized network—into a smaller model by training the small model to match the "soft targets" produced by the cumbersome model's softmax raised to a high temperature (e.g., T = 20 for MNIST).

papers.title: Layer Normalization
papers.pitch: This paper introduces layer normalization, a technique to accelerate the training of deep neural networks by normalizing the summed inputs to all neurons within a layer using statistics computed from a single training case—unlike batch normalization, which normalizes each neuron independently using statistics computed across a mini-batch.

papers.title: Wasserstein GAN
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the Wasserstein GAN (WGAN), an alternative to traditional GAN training that replaces the Jensen-Shannon divergence with the Earth-Mover (EM) distance — also called Wasserstein-1 — as the loss function.

papers.title: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning for Fast Adaptation of Deep Networks
papers.pitch: This paper proposes Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning (MAML), a meta-learning algorithm that trains a model's initial parameters such that a small number of gradient steps on a new task—using only a few datapoints—produces maximal generalization performance, effectively training the model to be easy to fine-tune.

papers.title: Prototypical Networks for Few-shot Learning
papers.pitch: This paper introduces prototypical networks for few-shot classification, a method that learns an embedding space where each class is represented by the mean of its support examples — the prototype — and classification proceeds by assigning query points to the nearest prototype via a softmax over distances.

papers.title: mixup: Beyond Empirical Risk Minimization
papers.pitch: This paper introduces mixup, a data-agnostic data augmentation principle that trains neural networks on convex combinations of random pairs of input vectors and their corresponding one-hot label encodings (sampling λ ~ Beta(α, α) to produce virtual examples $\tilde{x} = \lambda x_i + (1-\lambda)x_j$ and $\tilde{y} = \lambda y_i + (1-\lambda)y_j$).

papers.title: Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization
papers.pitch: This paper analyzes why adaptive gradient methods like Adam generalize worse than SGD with momentum on image classification tasks (CIFAR-10, ImageNet32x32 using ResNet architectures), diagnosing the root cause as the implicit coupling of L2 regularization into the adaptive gradient update, which unequally penalizes parameters proportionally to their gradient history rather than uniformly.

papers.title: Universal Language Model Fine-tuning for Text Classification
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Universal Language Model Fine-tuning (ULMFiT), a transfer learning method that applies a three-stage pipeline — general-domain language model pretraining, target-task LM fine-tuning with novel regularization, and classifier fine-tuning with gradual unfreezing — to achieve state-of-the-art text classification without task-specific architectures.

papers.title: Spectral Normalization for Generative Adversarial Networks
papers.pitch: This paper proposes a novel weight normalization technique called spectral normalization to stabilize the training of the discriminator in generative adversarial networks.

papers.title: The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis: Finding Sparse, Trainable Neural Networks
papers.pitch: This paper empirically studies whether dense, randomly-initialized neural networks contain sparse subnetworks that can train from scratch and match the full network's test accuracy.

papers.title: Group Normalization
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Group Normalization (GN) as a simple alternative to Batch Normalization that computes mean and variance within groups of channels rather than across the batch dimension (dividing channels into G groups and normalizing each group independently along the (H, W) axes).

papers.title: An Effective Approach to Unsupervised Machine Translation

papers.title: Large Batch Optimization for Deep Learning: Training BERT in 76 minutes
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the LAMB optimizer, a layerwise adaptive large batch optimization algorithm that scales training of attention-based models like BERT to batch sizes exceeding 32,000 without performance degradation, reducing BERT pretraining time from 3 days to just 76 minutes.

papers.title: Modifying Memories in Transformer Models
papers.pitch: This paper proposes a new task of explicitly modifying specific factual knowledge implicitly stored in Transformer language model parameters while preserving performance on unmodified facts.

papers.title: Contrastive Learning for Many-to-many Multilingual Neural Machine Translation
papers.pitch: This paper proposes mRASP2 (multilingual Contrastive Learning for Translation), a training method to build a single unified many-to-many multilingual neural machine translation model that prioritizes non-English translation quality.

papers.title: BitFit: Simple Parameter-efficient Fine-tuning for Transformer-based Masked Language-models
papers.pitch: This paper introduces BitFit (BIas-Term FIne-Tuning), a sparse fine-tuning method for pre-trained transformer masked language models where only the additive bias parameters—and optionally only a subset of them—are updated during task adaptation, while all weight matrices and gain parameters remain frozen at their pre-trained values.

papers.title: Finetuned Language Models Are Zero-Shot Learners
papers.pitch: This paper introduces a simple method for improving the zero-shot generalization of large language models.

papers.title: Few-Shot Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning is Better and Cheaper than In-Context Learning
papers.pitch: This paper introduces T-Few, a parameter-efficient few-shot learning recipe that directly challenges the dominance of in-context learning (ICL) by showing that fine-tuning a tiny fraction of parameters yields better accuracy at dramatically lower computational cost.

papers.title: LLaMA-Adapter: Efficient Fine-tuning of Language Models with Zero-init Attention
papers.pitch: This paper introduces LLaMA-Adapter, a lightweight parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that adapts the frozen LLaMA 7B model into an instruction-following model using only 1.2M learnable parameters—less than one hour of training on 8 A100 GPUs.

papers.title: Fine-Tuning Language Models with Just Forward Passes
papers.pitch: This paper proposes MeZO, a memory-efficient zeroth-order optimizer that adapts classical ZO-SGD to operate in-place, fine-tuning large language models with the same memory footprint as inference by reconstructing random perturbation vectors from saved random seeds rather than storing them.

papers.title: Full Parameter Fine-tuning for Large Language Models with Limited Resources

papers.title: DoLa: Decoding by Contrasting Layers Improves Factuality in Large Language Models
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Decoding by Contrasting Layers (DoLa), a simple decoding strategy for reducing hallucinations in pretrained large language models without requiring external knowledge retrieval or additional fine-tuning.

papers.title: LongLoRA: Efficient Fine-tuning of Long-Context Large Language Models
papers.pitch: LongLoRA introduces an efficient fine-tuning approach for extending the context sizes of pre-trained large language models, combining two complementary mechanisms: Shifted Sparse Attention (S2-Attn, which splits the context into groups and applies a half-head shift to enable inter-group information flow — approximating full attention with local computation) and an improved LoRA+ recipe

papers.title: VeRA: Vector-based Random Matrix Adaptation

papers.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization: Eliciting Strong Capabilities With Weak Supervision
papers.pitch: This paper studies whether weak model supervision can elicit the full capabilities of a much stronger model — an analogy for the core superalignment challenge of humans supervising superhuman models.

papers.title: GaLore: Memory-Efficient LLM Training by Gradient Low-Rank Projection
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Gradient Low-Rank Projection (GaLore), a memory-efficient training strategy that enables full-parameter learning by projecting weight gradients into a low-rank subspace during optimization — rather than constraining the weight matrices themselves to be low-rank as LoRA does.

papers.title: LoHan: Low-Cost High-Performance Framework to Fine-Tune 100B Model on a Consumer GPU

papers.title: Adam-mini: Use Fewer Learning Rates To Gain More

papers.title: Multi-Layer Transformers Gradient Can be Approximated in Almost Linear Time

papers.title: No More Adam: Learning Rate Scaling at Initialization is All You Need
