Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting
papers.pitch: This paper introduces dropout, a regularization technique that prevents neural networks from overfitting by randomly dropping units—along with their connections—during training (sampling an exponential number of “thinned” sub-networks at each weight update), then approximating the effect of averaging all those sub-networks at test time by simply using a single unthinned network with scaled-dow

papers.title: Understanding the difficulty of training deep feedforward neural networks
papers.pitch: This paper analyzes why standard gradient descent from random initialization fails to train deep feedforward neural networks, using supervised multi-layer perceptrons with one to five hidden layers on Shapeset-3×2, MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Small-ImageNet.

papers.title: Adapting Large Language Models for Document-Level Machine Translation
papers.pitch: This study empirically analyzes how to adapt moderately-sized large language models (7B parameters) for document-level machine translation (DOCMT) through task-specific fine-tuning.

papers.title: Semi-Supervised Learning Using Gaussian Fields and Harmonic Functions
papers.pitch: This paper introduces a semi-supervised learning framework based on a Gaussian random field model defined over a weighted graph connecting labeled and unlabeled instances, where the most probable configuration — the graph's harmonic function — has a unique closed-form solution efficiently computable via matrix methods or belief propagation.

papers.title: Least Angle Regression
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Least Angle Regression (LARS), a new model selection algorithm for linear regression that builds up coefficient estimates in a sequence of equiangular steps—each step moving along a direction that makes equal angles with the currently most correlated predictors.

papers.title: Regularized Multi-Task Learning
papers.pitch: This paper introduces a regularization-based multi–task learning method that extends single-task kernel methods—specifically Support Vector Machines—to learn multiple related tasks simultaneously by decomposing each task's model into a shared component and a task-specific deviation (operationalized via a task-coupling parameter μ in a novel matrix-valued kernel).

papers.title: On the importance of initialization and momentum in deep learning
papers.pitch: This paper analyzes how stochastic gradient descent with momentum can train deep neural networks and recurrent neural networks from random initializations — a feat previously thought to require sophisticated second-order methods like Hessian-Free optimization — by establishing that two mechanisms are jointly essential: a well-designed random initialization (the sparse initialization of Martens

papers.title: Pegasos: Primal Estimated sub-GrAdient SOlver for SVM
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Pegasos (Primal Estimated sub-GrAdient SOlver for SVM), a simple stochastic sub-gradient descent algorithm for solving the SVM optimization problem, and analyzes its convergence properties on standard benchmark datasets (astro-ph, CCAT, cov1, Reuters, Adult, USPS, MNIST).

papers.title: Random Forests
papers.pitch: This paper introduces random forests, a classifier consisting of an ensemble of tree-structured classifiers where each tree is grown using a random vector sampled independently from the same distribution, with the forest voting for the most popular class.

papers.title: Large-Scale Machine Learning with Stochastic Gradient Descent
papers.pitch: This paper analyzes why stochastic gradient descent (SGD) outperforms conventional optimization methods when training sets grow very large, using both theoretical asymptotic arguments and experiments on linear SVMs, CRFs, and the 2008 Pascal Large Scale Learning Challenge.

papers.title: Support Vector Machine Learning for Interdependent and Structured Output Spaces
papers.pitch: This paper introduces a Support Vector Machine learning formulation for interdependent and structured output spaces, generalizing multiclass SVMs to problems where the output Y consists of complex, structured objects — such as sequences, trees, or alignments — rather than interchangeable class labels.

papers.title: Going Deeper with Convolutions
papers.pitch: Introduces the Inception architecture (exemplified by the 22-layer GoogLeNet) that packs multi-scale convolutional filters (1×1, 3×3, 5×5) and parallel pooling into modular “Inception” blocks, using 1×1 convolutions for dimension reduction to approximate sparse connectivity while remaining hardware‑efficient. This yields state‑of‑the‑art ImageNet classification and detection accuracy while keeping

papers.title: SliceGPT: Compress Large Language Models by Deleting Rows and Columns
papers.pitch: This paper introduces SliceGPT, a post-training model compression method that reduces the size of large language models by deleting entire rows and columns of weight matrices — effectively lowering the embedding dimension of the network — rather than inducing unstructured or semi-structured sparsity.

papers.title: LLMLingua-2: Data Distillation for Efficient and Faithful Task-Agnostic Prompt Compression
papers.pitch: This paper introduces LLMLingua-2, a task-agnostic prompt compression method that reformulates compression as a binary token classification problem — preserving or discarding each word — trained via a data distillation procedure that extracts compression knowledge from GPT-4 into an extractive dataset built from MeetingBank transcripts.

papers.title: Let the Expert Stick to His Last: Expert-Specialized Fine-Tuning for Sparse Architectural Large Language Models
papers.pitch: This paper proposes Expert-Specialized Fine-Tuning (ESFT), a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language models that selectively tunes only the experts most relevant to a downstream task while freezing all other parameters.

papers.title: Addition is All You Need for Energy-efficient Language Models
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the linear-complexity multiplication (L-Mul) algorithm, which approximates floating-point tensor multiplication using only integer addition operations — a radically simpler operation that on modern hardware costs roughly 1/37th the energy of an fp32 multiply.

papers.title: Stuffed Mamba: Oversized States Lead to the Inability to Forget
papers.pitch: This paper studies why Mamba-2 models fail to generalize to context lengths beyond their training length, diagnosing the root cause as a state overparameterization problem where the recurrent state is excessively large relative to the training context, allowing the model to achieve strong language modeling without learning to effectively forget past tokens.

papers.title: RWKV-7 "Goose" with Expressive Dynamic State Evolution
papers.pitch: This paper introduces RWKV-7 "Goose", a new recurrent sequence modeling architecture that generalizes the delta rule with vector-valued gating and in-context learning rates, achieving constant memory usage and constant inference time per token.

papers.title: VSA: Faster Video Diffusion with Trainable Sparse Attention
papers.pitch: This paper introduces VSA (Video Sparse Attention), a trainable, hardware-efficient sparse attention mechanism for video diffusion transformers (DiTs) that replaces the quadratic 3D full attention at both training and inference.

papers.title: SparseLoRA: Accelerating LLM Fine-Tuning with Contextual Sparsity
papers.pitch: This paper introduces SparseLoRA, a method that accelerates LLM fine-tuning by applying contextual sparsity—dynamically selecting a sparse subset of weights for loss and gradient computation based on the input sequence.

papers.title: Attention Residuals
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Attention Residuals (AttnRes), a mechanism that replaces the fixed, uniform accumulation of standard residual connections with learned softmax attention over preceding layer outputs — allowing each layer to selectively aggregate earlier representations with input-dependent weights (e.g., a layer can learn to attend more strongly to the embedding or to specific earlier lay

papers.title: Nemotron-Cascade 2: Post-Training LLMs with Cascade RL and Multi-Domain On-Policy Distillation
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Nemotron-Cascade 2, an open 30B Mixture-of-Experts model with 3B activated parameters post-trained using an expanded Cascade RL framework—sequentially applying domain-specific reinforcement learning stages (instruction-following RL, multi-domain RL, RLHF, long-context RL, code RL, and SWE RL)—integrated with multi-domain on-policy distillation (MOPD) from intermed

papers.title: FIPO: Eliciting Deep Reasoning with Future-KL Influenced Policy Optimization
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Future-KL Influenced Policy Optimization (FIPO), a reinforcement learning algorithm that modifies the GRPO policy update by incorporating a discounted future-KL divergence term — creating a token-level credit assignment mechanism that re-weights advantages based on how each token influences subsequent trajectory behavior (e.g., amplifying the gradient for tokens that anch

papers.title: TAPS: Task Aware Proposal Distributions for Speculative Sampling
papers.pitch: This paper studies how the training distribution of lightweight draft models affects speculative decoding quality, evaluating HASS and EAGLE-2 drafters trained on MathInstruct, ShareGPT, and mixed-data variants against a fixed Llama-3-8B-Instruct verifier on MT-Bench, GSM8K, MATH-500, and SVAMP.

papers.title: Unifying Group-Relative and Self-Distillation Policy Optimization via Sample Routing
papers.pitch: This paper proposes Sample-Routed Policy Optimization (SRPO), a unified on-policy framework that routes correct rollouts to Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) for reward-aligned reinforcement and failed rollouts to Self-Distillation Policy Optimization (SDPO) for dense logit-level correction, augmented by an entropy-aware dynamic weighting mechanism that suppresses unreliable high-entro

papers.title: InCoder-32B-Thinking: Industrial Code World Model for Thinking
papers.pitch: This paper proposes InCoder-32B-Thinking, a thinking-augmented code model that bridges general code intelligence and industrial software development by integrating two synergistic mechanisms: Error-driven Chain-of-Thought (ECoT) synthesis (generating reasoning traces that explicitly model multi-turn error-correction processes, such as diagnosing GPU shared-memory faults across successive k

papers.title: RAGEN-2: Reasoning Collapse in Agentic RL
papers.pitch: This paper identifies and analyzes a failure mode in multi-turn LLM agent reinforcement learning called template collapse, where reasoning appears diverse within any single input but becomes input-agnostic across different inputs—a form of degradation invisible to standard entropy-based stability metrics.

papers.title: Rethinking Generalization in Reasoning SFT: A Conditional Analysis on Optimization, Data, and Model Capability
papers.pitch: This paper studies how cross-domain generalization in reasoning supervised fine-tuning (SFT) is jointly shaped by optimization dynamics, training data, and base model capability, conducting experiments on MATH500, AIME24, and OOD reasoning benchmarks using Qwen3-14B/8B-Base and InternLM2.5-20B-Base models.

papers.title: Nemotron 3 Super: Open, Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Model for Agentic Reasoning
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Nemotron 3 Super, a 120B-total-parameter (12B active) hybrid Mamba-Attention Mixture-of-Experts model pre-trained on 25 trillion tokens in NVFP4 precision with LatentMoE — a novel MoE architecture that projects tokens into a lower-dimensional latent space for routing and expert computation (reducing per-expert weight loads and all-to-all traffic by a factor $d/\ell$ while

papers.title: Rethinking On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models: Phenomenology, Mechanism, and Recipe
papers.pitch: This paper systematically studies the training dynamics of on-policy distillation (OPD) for large language models, analyzing a range of teacher–student configurations—including Qwen3-1.7B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-1.5B/7B, and their RL-fine-tuned variants—on mathematical reasoning benchmarks (AIME 2024/2025, AMC 2023).

papers.title: Translating Embeddings for Modeling Multi-relational Data
papers.pitch: This paper introduces TransE, an energy-based model for learning low-dimensional embeddings of multi-relational data that models relationships as translations operating on entity embeddings—if a triplet (head, label, tail) holds, then the head embedding plus the relationship vector should be close to the tail embedding (h + ℓ ≈ t).

papers.title: Rich feature hierarchies for accurate object detection and semantic segmentation
papers.pitch: This paper introduces R-CNN: Regions with CNN features, a simple and scalable object detection algorithm that bridges the gap between high-capacity convolutional neural networks for image classification and the task of object localization.

papers.title: Visualizing and Understanding Convolutional Networks
papers.pitch: This paper introduces a novel visualization technique that reveals the input stimuli exciting individual feature maps at any layer of a convolutional network, using a multi-layered Deconvolutional Network (deconvnet) to project feature activations back to the input pixel space.

papers.title: OverFeat: Integrated Recognition, Localization and Detection using Convolutional Networks
papers.pitch: This paper introduces OverFeat, an integrated framework that uses a single convolutional network to simultaneously perform classification, localization, and detection by processing images through a multi-scale sliding window approach.

papers.title: Very Deep Convolutional Networks for Large-Scale Image Recognition
papers.pitch: This paper systematically investigates how convolutional network depth affects accuracy in large-scale image recognition by evaluating architectures built exclusively from small 3×3 convolutional filters, stacked to increasing depths of 11–19 weight layers on the ILSVRC-2012 benchmark.

papers.title: Delving Deep into Rectifiers: Surpassing Human-Level Performance on ImageNet Classification
papers.pitch: This paper introduces two techniques for improving deep convolutional neural networks driven specifically by rectifier nonlinearities: the Parametric Rectified Linear Unit (PReLU) (a learned activation function that generalizes ReLU by adaptively learning the negative-part slope per channel, adding negligible parameters) and a rectifier-aware weight initialization method (a derivation of t

papers.title: DRAW: A Recurrent Neural Network For Image Generation
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the Deep Recurrent Attentive Writer (DRAW) architecture for image generation, which combines a sequential variational auto-encoding framework with a novel differentiable spatial attention mechanism that mimics the foveation of the human eye.

papers.title: FaceNet: A Unified Embedding for Face Recognition and Clustering
papers.pitch: This paper introduces FaceNet, a system that directly learns a mapping from face images to a compact Euclidean space where squared L2 distances correspond to face similarity, replacing the indirect bottleneck-layer representations used by prior deep learning face recognition systems.

papers.title: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the U-Net architecture, a fully convolutional network designed for biomedical image segmentation that can be trained end-to-end from very few annotated images.

papers.title: Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Faster R-CNN, a unified object detection system that integrates a deep convolutional Region Proposal Network (RPN) with the Fast R-CNN detector, sharing full-image convolutional features so that region proposal computation becomes nearly cost-free.

papers.title: Spatial Transformer Networks
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the Spatial Transformer, a differentiable module that can be inserted into convolutional neural network architectures to actively spatially transform feature maps conditional on the input data itself, without any extra training supervision or modification to the optimization process.

papers.title: Instance Normalization: The Missing Ingredient for Fast Stylization
papers.pitch: This short note revisits the feed-forward stylization method of Ulyanov et al.

papers.title: PointNet: Deep Learning on Point Sets for 3D Classification and Segmentation
papers.pitch: This paper introduces PointNet, a novel deep neural network architecture that directly consumes raw point clouds—unordered sets of 3D points—without requiring conversion to intermediate representations like voxel grids or multi-view images, which introduce quantization artifacts and unnecessary data expansion.

papers.title: Feature Pyramid Networks for Object Detection
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the Feature Pyramid Network (FPN), a general-purpose architecture that builds multi-scale feature pyramids with rich semantics at all levels by leveraging the inherent pyramidal hierarchy of deep convolutional networks through a top-down pathway with lateral connections (upsampling semantically strong but spatially coarse feature maps and merging them with high-resolution

papers.title: Paying More Attention to Attention: Improving the Performance of Convolutional Neural Networks via Attention Transfer
papers.pitch: This paper proposes using attention transfer as a mechanism for improving the performance of a student convolutional neural network by forcing it to mimic the spatial attention maps of a more powerful teacher network (e.g., matching where a ResNet-34 focuses its activation-based attention when classifying images).

papers.title: Mask R-CNN
papers.pitch: Mask R-CNN introduces a conceptually simple and flexible framework for object instance segmentation that extends Faster R-CNN by adding a parallel branch for predicting object masks alongside the existing bounding-box classification and regression branches.

papers.title: Unpaired Image-to-Image Translation using Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Networks
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Networks (CycleGAN), a method for learning to translate images from a source domain to a target domain without any paired training examples.

papers.title: Focal Loss for Dense Object Detection
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the Focal Loss, a dynamically weighted cross-entropy loss that reshapes the standard classification objective to down-weight well-classified examples (multiplying the log loss by a modulating factor $(1-p_t)^\gamma$) and thereby prevents the vast number of easy background samples from dominating the gradient during training of dense one-stage detectors.

papers.title: Large Scale GAN Training for High Fidelity Natural Image Synthesis
papers.pitch: This paper studies how Generative Adversarial Networks benefit from scaling to unprecedented model sizes and batch sizes, training class-conditional GANs on ImageNet at resolutions up to 512×512 using up to 2× to 4× more parameters and 8× the batch size compared to prior art.

papers.title: Momentum Contrast for Unsupervised Visual Representation Learning
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Momentum Contrast (MoCo), a mechanism for unsupervised visual representation learning that builds a large and consistent dynamic dictionary for contrastive learning by maintaining encoded keys in a queue and updating the key encoder via a momentum-based moving average of the query encoder.

papers.title: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations
papers.pitch: This paper introduces SimCLR, a simple framework for contrastive learning of visual representations that systematically studies what design choices enable self-supervised pretraining to match supervised performance on ImageNet.

papers.title: NeRF: Representing Scenes as Neural Radiance Fields for View Synthesis
papers.pitch: This paper introduces a method for synthesizing photorealistic novel views of complex scenes from a sparse set of input RGB images by optimizing an underlying continuous volumetric scene function.

papers.title: End-to-End Object Detection with Transformers
papers.pitch: This paper introduces DEtection TRansformer (DETR), a new architecture that reformulates object detection as a direct set prediction problem, eliminating hand-designed components like non-maximum suppression and anchor generation.

papers.title: Bootstrap your own latent: A new approach to self-supervised Learning
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Bootstrap Your Own Latent (BYOL), a new self-supervised image representation learning algorithm that trains an online network to predict the representations of a target network — itself an exponential moving average of the online network — without using any negative pairs.

papers.title: Training data-efficient image transformers & distillation through attention
papers.pitch: This paper introduces DeiT (Data-efficient image Transformers), a training methodology that enables convolution-free vision transformers to achieve competitive accuracy on ImageNet-1k without the massive external datasets previously required, training on a single 8-GPU node in 2–3 days.

papers.title: Tokens-to-Token ViT: Training Vision Transformers from Scratch on ImageNet
papers.pitch: This paper proposes a Tokens-to-Token Vision Transformer (T2T-ViT) that can be trained from scratch on the midsize ImageNet dataset and outperform comparable CNNs — a feat the vanilla Vision Transformer (ViT) fails to achieve.

papers.title: Pyramid Vision Transformer: A Versatile Backbone for Dense Prediction without Convolutions
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the Pyramid Vision Transformer (PVT), a pure Transformer backbone designed to serve as a direct, convolution-free replacement for CNN backbones in dense prediction tasks.

papers.title: Coordinate Attention for Efficient Mobile Network Design
papers.pitch: This paper proposes coordinate attention, a novel light-weight attention mechanism for mobile networks that embeds positional information into channel attention by factorizing 2D global pooling into two parallel 1D feature encoding processes—aggregating features along the horizontal and vertical directions separately to produce direction-aware and position-sensitive attention maps (as opposed

papers.title: Swin Transformer: Hierarchical Vision Transformer using Shifted Windows
papers.pitch: This paper proposes the Swin Transformer, a general-purpose vision backbone that adapts the Transformer architecture to computer vision by introducing a hierarchical representation (building feature maps at multiple resolutions through patch merging, like ConvNets) and a shifted window based self-attention mechanism (computing attention within local, non-overlapping windows that shift

papers.title: MLP-Mixer: An all-MLP Architecture for Vision
papers.pitch: This paper introduces MLP-Mixer, a vision architecture built entirely from multi-layer perceptrons that eschews both convolutions and self-attention, decomposing image processing into two alternating operations: channel-mixing MLPs (applied independently to each spatial location, akin to 1×1 convolutions) and token-mixing MLPs (applied across all spatial locations for a single channel, akin to

papers.title: Florence: A New Foundation Model for Computer Vision
papers.pitch: This paper introduces Florence, a vision foundation model trained on 900 million Web-scale image-text pairs that expands learned visual representations from coarse scene-level features to fine-grained object-level features, from static images to dynamic videos, and from RGB to multiple modalities like caption and depth (via adapter modules: Dynamic Head, METER, and Video CoSwin).

papers.title: A ConvNet for the 2020s
papers.pitch: This paper analyzes how to modernize a standard ResNet architecture by systematically incorporating design choices from hierarchical vision Transformers, producing a family of pure ConvNet models called ConvNeXt.

papers.title: The geometry of hidden representations of large transformer models
papers.pitch: This paper shows that hidden representations in large self-supervised transformers undergo a consistent depth-wise pattern—an early intrinsic-dimension expansion, a strong compression into a low-ID region that best encodes semantic structure, and a final decoding phase—and links these geometric changes to local neighbor rearrangements. The key contribution is an unsupervised, geometry-based rule t

papers.title: DINOv2: Learning Robust Visual Features without Supervision
papers.pitch: This paper introduces DINOv2, a family of self-supervised vision transformer encoders that produce general-purpose visual features competitive with weakly-supervised alternatives across image and pixel-level tasks without any fine-tuning.

papers.title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
papers.pitch: This paper trains a large-scale deep convolutional neural network to classify the 1.2 million high-resolution images of the ImageNet LSVRC-2010 challenge into 1000 categories, achieving top-1 and top-5 test error rates of 37.5% and 17.0% — substantially below the prior state-of-the-art at 47.1% and 28.2%.

papers.title: DeCAF: A Deep Convolutional Activation Feature for Generic Visual Recognition
papers.pitch: This paper evaluates whether deep convolutional activation features—extracted from a supervised convolutional network trained on ILSVRC-2012 (ImageNet)—can serve as a generic visual representation for tasks with insufficient labeled data to train a full deep architecture from scratch.

papers.title: DeepFace: Closing the Gap to Human-Level Performance in Face Verification
papers.pitch: This paper introduces DeepFace, a face verification system that couples explicit 3D model-based frontalization with a nine-layer deep neural network trained on the largest facial dataset to date — 4.4 million labeled images across 4,030 identities.

papers.title: Histograms of Oriented Gradients for Human Detection
papers.pitch: This paper studies how to construct robust feature sets for visual object recognition by systematically evaluating Histograms of Oriented Gradient (HOG) descriptors for human detection using linear SVM classifiers on the MIT and INRIA pedestrian datasets.

papers.title: Distinctive Image Features from Scale-Invariant Keypoints
papers.pitch: This paper introduces the Scale Invariant Feature Transform (SIFT), a method for extracting distinctive image features that are invariant to image scaling and rotation and partially invariant to changes in illumination and 3D viewpoint.

papers.title: Rapid Object Detection using a Boosted Cascade of Simple Features
papers.pitch: This paper introduces a machine learning framework for extremely rapid visual object detection, demonstrated on frontal face detection.
